note: Tuning task overview knowledge base (Jira OVTASK overview rows, gates omitted). Curated by Turbine Control from the PLANC model, the Controller Description and CoPaD; text marked [P] is proposed and must be reviewed. Highly affected functionalities / by = tuning couplings (A -> B: changing the tunable parameters of A requires re-tuning or re-checking B), with the physical reason; not signal links.

tasks.name: Edgewise Synchronous Frequency Estimator (ESFE)
scope: Estimates online the 1st, 2nd and 3rd edgewise synchronous frequencies (1ES-3ES) of the rotor with a sliding discrete Fourier transform of the rotor speed, searching around an initial frequency within a frequency range; a sensitivity threshold decides when the estimate is updated.
The estimates place the edgewise notches of the Rotor Speed Filter, so that the edgewise modes of the blades are not fed back into the pitch and torque control.
kpi: - Estimated 1ES-3ES vs the modal frequencies of the aeroelastic model over the operating range (bias per wind bin).
- Stability of the estimate: no jumps to other spectral peaks (3P harmonics, tower or drivetrain modes), low scatter.
- Tracking when the frequencies shift (rotor speed, pitch, ice) and convergence time after start-up.
- [P] Residual edgewise content in the filtered rotor speed (DLC 1.2a).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a normal turbulence (the edgewise frequencies move with rotor speed and pitch; the estimate must stay locked over the whole operating range); DLC 1.7 OWI (ice mass lowers the edgewise frequencies: the estimate must follow, otherwise the notches miss the modes).
**Medium:** DLC 1.3 ETM (strong excitation and large pitch variation); DLC 3.1 start-up (initialisation while the rotor runs up).
**Lower:** DLC 2.1g / 2.5a grid faults (transient content may disturb the estimate briefly).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Rotor Speed Filter (OVTASK-121):** the 1ES-3ES band-stop filters are centred on the ESFE estimates: the frequency range, initial frequency and threshold of ESFE decide whether the notches sit on the actual edgewise modes. A notch off the mode leaves edgewise content in the speed feedback and adds phase lag at the wrong frequency.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Wrong initial frequency or range: the estimator locks on another peak and the speed-filter notches sit at the wrong frequency: edgewise content reaches the speed loop, with edgewise vibrations, pitch and torque activity and, in the worst case, coupling with the torque control.
Threshold too low: noisy, jumping estimate (moving notches add disturbance). Too high: no update when the frequencies shift (ice, temperature).

tasks.name: Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch Curve
scope: Defines the minimum pitch angle as a function of power in partial load (opti-pitch curve, maximum aerodynamic efficiency) and its variants: opti-pitch at curtailed speed, ACS and safe-mode pitch tables and air-density compensation.

Its output OptiPitchAngle is the base of the minimum pitch limit on which all load-handle offsets are added; it sets the aerodynamic operating point, and therefore thrust and power, below and around rated.
kpi: - Power curve / AEP and aerodynamic efficiency in partial load (DLC 1.2a, power-curve runs).
- Thrust and blade / tower loads in the transition to rated (thrust peak).
- [P] Margin to stall (angle of attack) and pitch activity around rated.
dlcs: **High:** power-curve runs and DLC 1.2a (efficiency in partial load and the thrust peak around rated, which drives tower and blade fatigue).
**Medium:** DLC 1.2c steep shear and DLC 1.3 ETM (operation near rated with high flap loads: the minimum pitch sets the thrust); DLC 2.4a/b extreme yaw error.
**Lower:** DLC 1.7 OWI (iced operation uses its own offsets).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Pitch Trajectory Offsets: Pitch Limit by Wind (PLBW) (OVTASK-138):** the pitch-limit-by-wind offsets (PLBW_Pit1 / 2) are added to the opti-pitch curve: a new curve changes the resulting minimum pitch and thrust.
- **Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch at Curtailed Speed (OPCS) (OVTASK-157):** the curtailed opti-pitch is derived from the same pitch tables; both must be consistent at the transition.
- **Power Estimator (OVTASK-142):** the running power curve of the estimator is computed with the opti-pitch curve.
- **Adaptive Control Strategy (ACS) (OVTASK-152):** the ACS pitch offsets (ACS_PitTbl_*) are added to the opti-pitch curve: the load reduction per offset depends on the pitch it starts from.

- **Speed-Pitch Controller: Aerodynamic Gain Scheduling (OVTASK-125):** the pitch at rated is the first point of the gain schedule: the aerodynamic sensitivity at the start of full load depends on it.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Air Density (OVTASK-338):** the opti-pitch curve and its air-density compensation depend on the density: the optimum pitch and the thrust at a given wind speed change with it.
- **Rotor Performance Data (OVTASK-345):** the optimal pitch per tip-speed ratio is the maximum of the power coefficient of the rotor tables.
- **Flex Configuration (OVTASK-307):** the rated power sets where the opti-pitch curve ends and pitch regulation starts.

- **Power Trajectory: Speed-Power Curve (OVTASK-308):** the curve sets the tip-speed ratio at each wind speed, and the optimal pitch is defined for that tip-speed ratio: curve and opti-pitch are designed together.
risk: Sub-optimal curve: AEP loss. Too low pitch near rated: thrust peak, higher flap and tower loads, stall risk in turbulence. Wrong curtailed-speed curve: loads or AEP loss in curtailed operation.

tasks.name: Active Drive Train Damper 2 (ADTD2)
scope: Damps drivetrain torsional oscillations: the measured generator speed on the low-speed side (GenSdSpd_ValueLSS) is high-pass filtered, phase-adjusted and notch-filtered at 3P, and fed back as an additional generator power / torque with the right phase to stabilise the torsional mode.
Purpose: reduce the fatigue of gearbox and shafts and avoid unstable drivetrain modes.
kpi: - Damping of the drivetrain torsional mode (logarithmic decrement / decay after a torque step).
- Gearbox and main-shaft torque fatigue (DEL) in DLC 1.2a.
- Power / torque ripple added by the damper and the share of converter margin it uses.
- No 3P torque injected; correct behaviour during and after grid faults.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a normal turbulence (torsional fatigue of the gearbox); DLC 2.1g grid drop and DLC 2.5a LVRT (the torque step excites the drivetrain mode; the damper must keep working, scaled, during and after the dip).
**Medium:** DLC 1.3 ETM; DLC 3.x / 4.x start-up and shut-down (torque transients).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Dynamic Power Envelope (OVTASK-143):** the power envelope reserves headroom for the damping power of ADTD2 (DynPwrEnv_ADTD*): the reserve is sized from the damping power the tuned ADTD2 needs.

- **Drive Train Oscillation Monitor (DTOM) (OVTASK-146):** the residual drivetrain oscillation after damping sets the normal level the oscillation monitor sees: its limits (DTOM_Str*_Lim) are set above that level.

- **Grid Fault Ride Through (GFRT) (OVTASK-301):** a grid fault excites the drivetrain mode; the damper gain during and after the fault (ADTD2_GainFactGFRT, GFRT_Post_ADTD2AccThres) and the post-fault power ramps are tuned together.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Grid Fault Ride Through (GFRT) (OVTASK-301):** the post-fault power recovery (GFRT_Post_* power limits and ramps) decides how much the drivetrain mode is excited after a grid fault, and so how much the drivetrain damper must act.
risk: Too little gain or wrong phase: poorly damped torsional mode, gearbox and shaft fatigue, possible instability. Too much gain: power ripple, grid flicker, interaction with the speed-power control. Wrong 3P notch: 3P torque injected.

tasks.name: Wind Speed Estimator
scope: Estimates the rotor-effective wind speed at standard air density, using the turbine as a sensor: collective pitch, rotor speed and power are inverted through the rotor performance (power-coefficient) tables.
Outputs (WinAvail__SpdRotEq, SpdEquiv, SpdFree, status) are used for gain scheduling, derating, available power and load estimation.
kpi: - Bias and scatter of the estimate vs the rotor-effective wind of the simulation per wind bin (DLC 1.2a).
- Dynamic tracking in gusts (DLC 1.4) and consistency with air-density and yaw-misalignment compensation.
- [P] Effect on the consumers: speed-pitch gain scheduling and high-wind derating thresholds.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a and power-curve runs (bias over the wind-speed range); DLC 1.4 ECD and 9.4 gusts (the estimate schedules the speed-pitch gains during the gust).
**Medium:** DLC 1.5 EWS and DLC 2.4a/b yaw error (inflow not seen by the tables); DLC 1.7 OWI (ice degrades the rotor performance, biasing the estimate).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller: Aerodynamic Gain Scheduling (OVTASK-125):** the estimated wind speed is a breakpoint of the gain schedule: an estimate bias moves the scheduled gain away from the actual operating point, mainly near rated where the aerodynamic sensitivity changes fastest.

- **Pitch Trajectory Offsets: Pitch Limit by Wind (PLBW) (OVTASK-138):** the pitch-limit-by-wind breakpoints (PLBW_WindSpd1 / 2) are defined on the estimated wind speed: a bias shifts the minimum pitch to other wind speeds, which changes thrust peaks and AEP.
- **Thrust Estimator (OVTASK-153):** the thrust estimate is a function of the estimated wind speed: its bias is passed on to the thrust.
- **Speed Limit by Power (SLP) (OVTASK-112):** the speed limit table (SLP_RotSpdTbl) is indexed with the estimated wind speed.
- **Rotor Performance Monitor (OVTASK-286):** the monitor compares the measured wind speed with the estimate: the normal error band (RotPerfM_WindSpdError*) depends on the accuracy of the estimator.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Air Density (OVTASK-338):** the aerodynamic power scales with air density: the density used in the inversion of the power table sets the bias of the wind speed estimate.

- **Rotor Performance Data (OVTASK-345):** the estimator inverts the rotor power table (RotPerfData_PwrTbl): any error of the aerodynamic table becomes a bias of the estimated wind speed over the whole range.
risk: Biased estimate: wrong speed-pitch gain scheduling (sluggish or unstable loop), wrong high-wind derating (AEP loss or high-wind loads), wrong available-power and thrust estimates for grid services and load functions.

tasks.name: Pitch Trajectory Offsets: Pitch Limit by Wind (PLBW)
scope: Builds the minimum pitch angle from the opti-pitch angle plus a set of offsets (load handles BLL / GILL, monitors, ice, yaw misalignment, inertial response, air-density compensation) and the Pitch Limit by Wind: a minimum pitch as a function of the highest measured wind speed.

PLBW protects against extreme blade loads with large yaw errors at high wind, when the measured wind is high but the opti-pitch would still allow a low pitch. The load offsets can also shift the collective pitch reference directly.
kpi: - Blade flap and tower extremes with large yaw error at high wind (DLC 2.4a/b) and in gusts.
- AEP / power-curve loss from PLBW activation in normal operation (DLC 1.2a).
- [P] Correct release of the limit after the wind drops (no lingering derating) and smooth combination of offsets.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.4a/b extreme yaw error (large yaw error at high wind: the case PLBW exists for); DLC 1.2a (activation in normal operation costs AEP).
**Medium:** DLC 1.3 ETM, DLC 1.4 ECD and DLC 9.4 (direction change with high wind); DLC 1.5 EWS.
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Blade Load Limiter (BLL) (OVTASK-127):** the minimum pitch at high wind reduces the thrust and the flapwise moment: BLL thresholds and gain act on the extremes left after this offset.

- **Gust Induced Load Limiter (GILL) (OVTASK-130):** the minimum pitch at high wind sets the flapwise load from which a gust starts: the gust load GILL must remove, and so its thresholds and gains, depend on this offset.
- **Power Boost (OVTASK-141):** the boost pitch offsets (PB_*_PitMinOff) are defined relative to the minimum pitch.
- **Speed Control Scheduler: Full Power State Machine (OVTASK-160):** the gap to the minimum pitch (FPSM_*_PitGapToMinPit) that decides the full-power state is measured from this minimum pitch.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Wind Speed Estimator (OVTASK-155):** the pitch-limit-by-wind breakpoints (PLBW_WindSpd1 / 2) are defined on the estimated wind speed: a bias shifts the minimum pitch to other wind speeds, which changes thrust peaks and AEP.

- **Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch Curve (OVTASK-140):** the pitch-limit-by-wind offsets (PLBW_Pit1 / 2) are added to the opti-pitch curve: a new curve changes the resulting minimum pitch and thrust.
risk: PLBW too low or too late: high flap and tower extremes with yaw error at high wind. Too high or too slow to release: unnecessary derating and AEP loss. Wrong combination of offsets: pitch steps, double counting of load offsets.

tasks.name: Individual Pitch Control (IPC)
scope: Reduces blade flap fatigue and the rotor tilt and yaw moments: the measured tilt and yaw moments are transformed into a cyclic (1P) pitch offset per blade (inverse Coleman transform with the rotor azimuth), with 3P mixing, amplitude limits and activation logic.
Trade-off: more pitch travel, hence more pitch bearing damage and actuator wear (tuned together with PDA).
kpi: - Blade flap and hub / yaw-bearing fatigue (DEL) and mean tilt / yaw moments (DLC 1.2a).
- Pitch bearing damage and pitch travel / rate (cost of IPC).
- Extreme tilt / yaw moments and blade loads in DLC 1.3, 1.4 and yaw error (DLC 2.4b).
- Amplitude saturation occupancy and activation / deactivation behaviour.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a normal turbulence (shear, tilt and turbulence create 1P blade load variations: the fatigue IPC removes, and the pitch bearing damage it costs); DLC 2.4b extreme yaw error at high wind (large yaw / tilt moments).
**Medium:** DLC 1.3 ETM and DLC 1.4 ECD (extreme rotor moments); DLC 1.2c steep shear (large 1P loading).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Tip to Tower Clearance Controller (TTCC) (OVTASK-128):** IPC reduces the 1P flapwise and tilt loads and changes the blade deflection at the tower passage: the TTCC load thresholds and pitch offset are set with IPC active.
- **Pitch Damage Attenuator (PDA) (OVTASK-136):** IPC is the largest source of pitch travel and bearing damage: the PDA activation and attenuation are tuned for the IPC amplitude.
- **Controller Safe Mode (OVTASK-129):** the safe-mode derating when IPC is unavailable (SafeMode_IPC_*) must compensate the load reduction the tuned IPC gives.
- **Controller Functionality Scheduler (OVTASK-135):** the IPC pitch amplitudes allowed per state (FuncSche_IPCAllowedPitAmp*) are set from the amplitude the tuned IPC needs.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Rotor Azimuth Estimator and Monitor (OVTASK-334):** IPC transforms the blade moments to tilt / yaw and back with the rotor azimuth: an azimuth offset or delay rotates the tilt / yaw axes, so the IPC gain and phase are only valid for a correct azimuth.
- **Pitch Servo Controller (PSC) (OVTASK-132):** IPC commands 1P / 2P cyclic pitch: the actuator must follow at those frequencies, and its phase lag there sets the phase compensation and gain of IPC.
- **Pitch Reference Limiter (OVTASK-296):** the same rate limit applies to collective plus cyclic pitch: it bounds the IPC amplitude that can be added at high collective activity.
risk: Too little IPC: higher blade flap and yaw / tilt fatigue. Too much: pitch bearing damage and actuator wear above design, interaction with PDA and TTCC. Wrong azimuth phase: IPC adds load instead of removing it.

tasks.name: Tip to Tower Clearance Controller (TTCC)
scope: Prevents blade-tower strikes: when the load level indicates a risk, it pitches out the blade that is about to pass in front of the tower, unloading it and increasing the tip-to-tower clearance.
Activation from the filtered average out-of-plane and tilt moments (load level) and from the blade azimuth (window in front of the tower).
kpi: - Minimum tip-to-tower clearance (ULS) in DLC 1.2c steep shear, DLC 1.5 EWS and the turbulent load cases, with and without TTCC.
- AEP loss and pitch activity / pitch bearing damage caused by TTCC.
- Activation statistics vs wind speed (only where clearance is at risk).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2c steep shear and DLC 1.5 EWS (positive shear bends the top blade towards the tower: minimum clearance); DLC 1.2a and its DLC 1.1 extrapolation (extreme deflection in normal turbulence).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Pitch Damage Attenuator (PDA) (OVTASK-136):** TTCC pitch offsets add pitch travel per revolution in the tower passage: PDA must account for them.
- **Controller Functionality Scheduler (OVTASK-135):** the maximum TTCC offset (TTCC_PitOffsetMax) in the scheduler bounds the TTCC action.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Rotor Azimuth Estimator and Monitor (OVTASK-334):** the tower-passage window (TTCC_ActivationLvl_AziStart / AziEnd) is defined in azimuth: azimuth errors move the window away from the real tower passage.
- **Pitch Servo Controller (PSC) (OVTASK-132):** TTCC compensates the time the actuator needs to pitch out before the tower passage (TTCC_DelayPit): a slower or faster actuator changes that delay.

- **Individual Pitch Control (IPC) (OVTASK-133):** IPC reduces the 1P flapwise and tilt loads and changes the blade deflection at the tower passage: the TTCC load thresholds and pitch offset are set with IPC active.
risk: Too late or too weak: blade-tower strike risk, clearance below the design limit (already flagged as critical by Loads). Too early or too strong: AEP loss, pitch activity and bearing damage. Wrong azimuth timing: pitch-out on the wrong blade.

tasks.name: Pitch Damage Attenuator (PDA)
scope: Reduces pitch bearing damage, which grows with the cube of the bearing moment times the pitch travel: PDA limits the pitch movement of the blade(s) more heavily loaded than the others, from the mean and fluctuating pitch bearing moments.
Activation depends on bearing moment level, rotor speed, pitch rate and pitch imbalance.
kpi: - Pitch bearing damage (moment^3 x travel) per blade in DLC 1.2a vs no PDA.
- Side effects on blade and hub loads and on speed control (pitch travel limited).
- Activation level statistics and interaction with IPC / TTCC.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a normal turbulence (pitch bearing fatigue accumulates in normal operation, especially with IPC active).
**Medium:** DLC 1.2c steep shear (large and unequal blade moments); DLC 1.3 ETM (high pitch activity).
**Lower:** DLC 1.4 ECD (extremes: PDA must not reduce protection).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Controller Functionality Scheduler (OVTASK-135):** the PDA activation level in operation (FuncSche_PDAActivationLevelOperat) and its priority against BLL / GILL depend on how much pitch travel PDA removes.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the collective pitch activity of the speed loop is the main source of pitch bearing damage at high wind: the PDA activation thresholds (pitch speed, bearing moment) depend on it.
- **Individual Pitch Control (IPC) (OVTASK-133):** IPC is the largest source of pitch travel and bearing damage: the PDA activation and attenuation are tuned for the IPC amplitude.
- **Tip to Tower Clearance Controller (TTCC) (OVTASK-128):** TTCC pitch offsets add pitch travel per revolution in the tower passage: PDA must account for them.
risk: Too little action: pitch bearing damage above design (raised by IPC). Too much: blade and hub loads increase and the speed control loses pitch authority (overspeed risk).

tasks.name: High Wind Operator (HWO)
scope: Curtails power and rotor speed as a function of the estimated wind speed before the high-wind cut-out, so that the turbine keeps producing (grid compliance, no abrupt cut-out) while the loads at very high wind stay within the design.
Outputs the power and speed reductions (HWO_PwrRed, HWO_SpdRed) to the Reduction Interface and ACS.
kpi: - Power and speed vs wind speed above the start of curtailment and at cut-out (production kept, no abrupt stops).
- Extreme and fatigue loads at high wind (DLC 1.2a / 1.3 at 20-25+ m/s) with the curtailment trajectory.
- [P] Number of cut-outs / restarts in high-wind time series and hysteresis behaviour.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a and DLC 1.3 ETM at high wind speeds (loads and production along the curtailment trajectory); DLC 2.4b extreme yaw error at 21-25 m/s (high-wind operation with large yaw error).
**Medium:** DLC 1.4 / 9.4 gusts at high wind (curtailed speed reference during the gust).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller: Aerodynamic Gain Scheduling (OVTASK-125):** the high-wind curtailment adds operating points (reduced speed and power at high pitch) that the gain schedule must cover with margin.

- **Wind Speed Monitor (OVTASK-290):** the wind limits for stop and restart (WL_High_*) must be consistent with the HWO cut-out window (HWO_*Cutout*, WindSpdCurtWinWidth): otherwise the turbine stops before or after HWO has curtailed.
- **Controller Overspeed Monitor (OVTASK-123):** the curtailed speed references at high wind change the reference against which the relative overspeed limits are set.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Curtailment too late or too weak: high loads at very high wind or more cut-outs. Too early or too strong: AEP loss. Wrong wind-speed filtering: oscillating references (pitch and power activity) near the thresholds.

tasks.name: Power Estimator
scope: Calculates the running power curve from the current operational settings (speed-power curve, opti-pitch curve, design power and speed) and estimates the possible (available) power from the estimated wind speed.
The available power is used by grid functions and park control (possible power, curtailment, grid faults).
kpi: - Available power vs the power the turbine actually produces in unconstrained operation (bias / scatter per wind bin, DLC 1.2a and power-curve runs).
- Correct update of the running power curve when settings change (opti-pitch, speed-power curve, rating).
- [P] Accuracy in curtailed operation (where possible power cannot be measured).
dlcs: **High:** power-curve runs and DLC 1.2a (accuracy of the possible power over the wind range).
**Medium:** curtailed operation (DLC 9.7 curtailed operation; derated cases), DLC 2.1g / 2.5a grid faults (available power used by GFRT).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Low Power Detector (OVTASK-278):** the low-power detection compares the produced power with a percentage of the expected power: the margin (LPDC_*PercentOfPwrCrv) must cover the error of the expected power.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Rotor Performance Data (OVTASK-345):** the available power is computed from the rotor power table: table errors appear directly in the estimate.
- **Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch Curve (OVTASK-140):** the running power curve of the estimator is computed with the opti-pitch curve.
risk: Biased available power: wrong possible-power reporting to the park / grid operator, wrong power reserve in grid functions, false low-power or ice detections.

tasks.name: Power Boost
scope: Increases power and rotor speed above their rated / design values above rated wind speed when the operating conditions allow it (ambient temperature, turbulence, pitch reference, grid power factor, no safe mode, ACS and curtailment conditions), to gain energy.
Outputs the active boosted rated power and speed (ActBoost_PwRated / SpdRated) used by the reduction interface and the speed-power control.
kpi: - AEP gain vs no boost and the loads increase it causes (fatigue and extremes above rated, DLC 1.2a / 1.3).
- Correct enabling / disabling with the criteria (temperature, turbulence, pitch) and smooth ramps.
- [P] Margin to the electrical limits of generator and converter while boosting.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a above rated (where boost runs: AEP gain and fatigue increase); DLC 1.3 ETM (turbulence criterion must disable boost).
**Medium:** DLC 2.3 and 4.2 with EOG (boost is disabled in these cases: transition behaviour); DLC 1.4 ECD.
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Adaptive Control Strategy (ACS) (OVTASK-152):** boost raises power and loads: ACS must curtail correctly in boosted operation.
- **Dynamic Power Envelope (OVTASK-143):** the boosted power level must fit inside the power envelope and its headroom.

- **Speed Control Scheduler: Full Power State Machine (OVTASK-160):** the full-power state uses gaps to minimum pitch per boost type (FPSM_BoostTyp*_PitGapToMinPit): they are set for the boost pitch offsets.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Rotor Performance Data (OVTASK-345):** the boost criteria use the rotor power table to judge the margin to rated power and loads.
- **Flex Configuration (OVTASK-307):** boost levels and conditions are defined relative to the rated power and speed.
- **Pitch Trajectory Offsets: Pitch Limit by Wind (PLBW) (OVTASK-138):** the boost pitch offsets (PB_*_PitMinOff) are defined relative to the minimum pitch.
risk: Boost too aggressive or criteria too loose: loads and component temperatures above design. Too conservative: AEP loss. Wrong ramps: power / speed steps.

tasks.name: Thrust Estimator
scope: Estimates the rotor thrust from collective pitch, rotor speed and estimated wind speed through the rotor thrust tables (with air-density correction), normalised by the nominal thrust.
Used by load-estimating and load-limiting functions.
kpi: - Estimated vs simulated rotor thrust (bias / scatter per wind bin, DLC 1.2a) and in gusts (DLC 1.4).
- Correct normalisation (nominal thrust) for the consumers.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a (static accuracy over the wind range, including the thrust peak near rated).
**Medium:** DLC 1.4 ECD and DLC 1.3 ETM (dynamic accuracy in gusts and turbulence).
**Lower:** DLC 1.7 OWI (iced rotor changes the thrust tables).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Gust Induced Load Limiter (GILL) (OVTASK-130):** GILL is gain-scheduled with the normalised thrust estimate: its gains are only valid if the thrust estimate is correct at the gust conditions.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Rotor Performance Data (OVTASK-345):** the thrust estimate is read from the rotor thrust table (RotPerfData_ThrustTbl, ThrustNom).
- **Wind Speed Estimator (OVTASK-155):** the thrust estimate is a function of the estimated wind speed: its bias is passed on to the thrust.
risk: Biased thrust: ACS load estimates wrong (unneeded curtailment or loads above design in curtailed operation).

tasks.name: Tower Acceleration Limiter (TAL)
scope: Attenuates tower fore-aft oscillations by limiting the pitch rate: from the fore-aft nacelle acceleration (band-limited around the tower frequency), the operating state and the collective pitch it computes a pitch-rate gain for the pitch control states.
It targets mainly stops, where a fast pitch-out after a thrust peak drives the tower bottom fore-aft extreme.
kpi: - Tower-base fore-aft extremes in stops and shut-downs (DLC 4.x, 5.1, 2.x with stop) and in gusts with stop (DLC 2.3).
- Stopping time and rotor overspeed during the stop (a slower pitch-out must not cause overspeed).
- Activation statistics in normal operation (DLC 1.2a: minimal).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.3 EOG with grid drop and DLC 4.2 EOG shut-down (thrust drops while the tower is moving: the tower swings back and the fore-aft extreme is set); DLC 5.1 emergency shut-down; DLC 2.1 faults with stop.
**Medium:** DLC 4.1 normal shut-down; DLC 1.3 ETM (tower oscillation in operation).
**Lower:** DLC 1.2a (must not act in normal operation).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Controller Overspeed Monitor (OVTASK-123):** TAL slows the pitch-out when the tower accelerates, also in stops: slower pitch-out gives higher speed peaks, which the overspeed limits must accept.

- **Tower Vibration Monitor (OVTASK-310):** TAL limits the tower acceleration: the vibration-monitor limits must sit above the TAL activation levels so that TAL acts before the monitor stops the turbine.
- **Adaptive Control Strategy (ACS) (OVTASK-152):** TAL and ACS both react to tower acceleration: the ACS escalation levels are set above the TAL action.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Pitch Control States: General Pitch Rate Limits (OVTASK-131):** TAL reduces the positive pitch-rate limit (SpdPit_MaxPitRefRatePosLoadRed): its effect is relative to the general limit.

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the tower fore-aft motion that TAL reacts to is driven by the thrust changes the speed loop makes: a faster loop excites or damps the tower 1st fore-aft mode differently, so the TAL activation levels must be re-set.
risk: Too little action: high tower fore-aft extremes in stops. Too much: pitch-out too slow in stops, overspeed and longer stopping, higher blade loads during the stop.

tasks.name: Safety System Overspeed (SRSG)
scope: Secondary protection layer against overspeed: the safety system (SRSG and LMU) stops the turbine independently of the controller when the rotor speed exceeds its limits. Turbine Control owns the speed thresholds of the safety system together with the Safety team.
The thresholds must sit above the controller overspeed monitor (primary layer) and below the design overspeed of the structure.
kpi: - Maximum rotor speed in all load cases vs the SRSG / LMU thresholds (no safety trip in normal or extreme operation; trip in the overspeed fault cases).
- Order of the layers: controller overspeed monitor < SRSG < design overspeed.
- Extremes in the safety-system stop cases (DLC 2.2).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.1c controller overspeed and DLC 2.2 safety-system overspeed (the safety layer must stop the turbine when the controller fails); DLC 2.1g grid drop and DLC 2.3 EOG with grid drop (highest speed peaks without torque).
**Medium:** DLC 1.4 ECD, DLC 1.5 EWS, DLC 9.4 extreme gusts (must not trip the safety system).
affects: None to a high degree: its parameters only set alarm / stop limits; they do not change how other functions control the turbine (a wrong limit gives false or late stops, not a different tuning).
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Controller Overspeed Monitor (OVTASK-123):** the safety-system overspeed limits must sit above the controller limits, with margin, so that the controller protection acts first.
risk: Too low: safety trips in normal or extreme operation (hard stops, high loads, availability loss). Too high: no independent protection before the design overspeed; certification non-compliance.

tasks.name: Dynamic Power Envelope
scope: Limits the power reference to what converter, generator and electrical hardware can deliver at the instantaneous rotor speed (power envelope vs speed, short-term peak envelope), and reserves power margin for the active dampers (ADTD2, side-side tower damper).
The active envelope (ActPwrEnv_Power / Speed) is the power-speed boundary used by the speed-power control and many operational functions.
kpi: - Envelope consistent with the electrical capability statement of generator and converter (no limit exceeded, no unnecessary margin).
- AEP / power curve with the envelope active; behaviour in grid faults and reduced-converter operation.
- Power margin left for ADTD2 and the tower damper.
dlcs: **High:** power-curve runs and DLC 1.2a (operation along the envelope in partial and full load); DLC 2.5a LVRT / grid faults (peak envelope and damper margins during the dip).
**Medium:** DLC 1.3 ETM (speed excursions along the envelope); start-up / shut-down (low-speed part of the envelope).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Speed-Power Controller (PI) (OVTASK-159):** the power envelope bounds the power reference the speed-power loop can command: power headroom and rates change the loop behaviour at the limits.
- **Adaptive Control Strategy (ACS) (OVTASK-152):** the power envelope limits the power ACS starts from when it curtails: the load reduction per curtailment level depends on it.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Active Drive Train Damper 2 (ADTD2) (OVTASK-292):** the power envelope reserves headroom for the damping power of ADTD2 (DynPwrEnv_ADTD*): the reserve is sized from the damping power the tuned ADTD2 needs.

- **Active Tower Damper Side-Side (ATD) (OVTASK-148):** the power envelope reserves headroom for the damping power of the side-side tower damper (ATD_X_MaxPwr and the ATD power estimate in the envelope): the reserve is sized from the power the tuned damper needs.
- **Active Drive Train Damper (ADTD, legacy) (OVTASK-145):** when the legacy damper is the active one, its power saturation (ADTD_PwrSat) is the damping power the envelope must reserve.
- **Power Boost (OVTASK-141):** the boosted power level must fit inside the power envelope and its headroom.
risk: Envelope above the hardware capability: converter / generator overload and trips. Too conservative: AEP loss and less margin for the speed control (overspeed risk) and dampers.

tasks.name: Adaptive Control Strategy (ACS)
scope: Tailors the turbine operation to the site loads: representative load estimators built from measured signals (thrust, tilt / yaw moments, nacelle accelerations, wind, turbulence, tower frequency) decide when to curtail power / speed or offset the pitch, so that the loads stay within the design while energy is maximised.
Outputs power and speed reductions to the Reduction Interface, pitch-table offsets and a boost disable.
kpi: - Load-estimator accuracy vs simulated loads (tower, blade, hub) in DLC 1.2 / 1.3.
- Load reduction achieved vs AEP lost when ACS acts (DLC 1.3 ETM with ACS active).
- No unnecessary activation in normal turbulence (DLC 1.2a).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.3 ETM (the only extreme case where ACS acts, with thresholds x1.22 for estimator uncertainty: the loads ACS must reduce); DLC 1.2a (activation and AEP cost in normal turbulence).
**Medium:** DLC 2.2x ETM with ACS failure (loads if ACS does not act); site-specific turbulence / wake cases.
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch Curve (OVTASK-140):** the ACS pitch offsets (ACS_PitTbl_*) are added to the opti-pitch curve: the load reduction per offset depends on the pitch it starts from.
- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the tower and blade load levels ACS reacts to are set by the speed-loop response: the escalation thresholds must be set on the final loop.
- **Tower Acceleration Limiter (TAL) (OVTASK-139):** TAL and ACS both react to tower acceleration: the ACS escalation levels are set above the TAL action.
- **Power Boost (OVTASK-141):** boost raises power and loads: ACS must curtail correctly in boosted operation.
- **Dynamic Power Envelope (OVTASK-143):** the power envelope limits the power ACS starts from when it curtails: the load reduction per curtailment level depends on it.
risk: Estimators not matched to the rotor: ACS curtails when not needed (AEP loss) or does not act when loads exceed the design (site suitability not ensured). Thresholds wrong: frequent activation, oscillating references.

tasks.name: Pitch Servo Controller (PSC)
scope: Controls the pitch position of each blade so that it tracks its pitch reference: a position loop on the hydraulic cylinder (piston length to pitch angle), with gain scheduling on pitch position and direction and band-stop / low-pass filters on the feedback.
Its bandwidth and phase are part of every pitch-based loop (speed-pitch, IPC, load handles).
kpi: - Tracking error and bandwidth / phase lag of pitch angle vs reference (step and chirp responses, DLC 1.2a time series).
- Pitch-rate and valve saturation occupancy; no oscillation at structural frequencies (blade edgewise, rotor modes).
- [P] Effect on the speed-loop margin and on IPC / PDA effectiveness.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a (continuous pitch activity: tracking, valve wear, interaction with the blade modes); DLC 1.4 ECD and DLC 2.1g / 2.5a (fast large pitch steps when the speed loop reacts to a gust or a torque loss).
**Medium:** DLC 4.x / 5.1 shut-downs (maximum pitch rate towards feather).
**Lower:** DLC 2.2 pitch runaway cases (fault handling is in the safety chain).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the pitch actuator is inside the speed loop: its bandwidth, deadband and gain schedule (PSC_Kp, Ki, KpDeadband, filters) add phase lag at the speed-loop crossover and limit the PI gains that keep a stability margin.

- **Individual Pitch Control (IPC) (OVTASK-133):** IPC commands 1P / 2P cyclic pitch: the actuator must follow at those frequencies, and its phase lag there sets the phase compensation and gain of IPC.

- **Tip to Tower Clearance Controller (TTCC) (OVTASK-128):** TTCC compensates the time the actuator needs to pitch out before the tower passage (TTCC_DelayPit): a slower or faster actuator changes that delay.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Too slow or too much phase lag: reduced stability margin of the speed loop, less effective load handles, overspeed peaks. Too aggressive: valve and actuator wear, oscillations, excitation of blade modes.

tasks.name: Speed-Power Controller (PI)
scope: Controls the rotor speed with the generator power (torque) in partial load (regions 1-2) up to design speed and rated power: a PI on the filtered rotor speed tracking the speed reference of the speed-power curve, with power limits from the active power envelope, ramp limits and grid-fault / inertial-response overrides.
Its power reference sets the partial-load operating point and the drivetrain torque dynamics.
kpi: - Speed tracking (mean / std per wind bin) and power curve / AEP in partial load (DLC 1.2a, power-curve runs).
- Drivetrain torque fluctuations and fatigue; power ramp rates within grid requirements.
- Smooth transition to the speed-pitch controller at rated and behaviour after grid faults.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a and power-curve runs (partial-load speed regulation, AEP and drivetrain fatigue).
**Medium:** DLC 2.1g / 2.5a grid faults (power reference recovery after the dip); DLC 3.x start-up (ramp to the speed-power curve).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the speed-power loop bandwidth at rated sets the speed excursions the speed-pitch loop meets at the transition from partial to full load.
- **Speed-Power Controller: Gain Scheduling (OVTASK-161):** the gain schedule is relative to the speed-power PI gains: changing Kp changes the gain at every scheduled speed.

- **Resonance Speed Avoider (RSA) (OVTASK-162):** in partial load the speed-power loop crosses the RSA window: its bandwidth and power rate limits set the crossing time and the power drop RSA_MinPwrReq must allow.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Power Trajectory: Speed-Power Curve (OVTASK-308):** the speed-power curve is the trajectory the speed-power loop follows in partial load: its slope sets the loop gain needed and the torque the drivetrain sees.

- **Rotor Speed Filter (OVTASK-121):** the phase lag of the speed filters at the crossover of the speed-power PI in partial load limits the gain that keeps a stability margin: changing the filters requires re-checking the PI gains.

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** near rated both loops are active around the transition: their bandwidths and the speed shift between their references decide whether they hand over smoothly or fight each other.

- **Speed Control Scheduler: Speed Shifter (OVTASK-163):** the speed shift between the pitch and power speed references (SpdShift_*) decides at which speed torque stops increasing and pitch takes over: it changes the speed-power loop behaviour near rated.

- **Speed-Power Controller: Gain Scheduling (OVTASK-161):** the gain schedule sets the effective loop gain of the speed-power PI over the partial-load speed range: changing it changes the loop margins at every speed.
- **Dynamic Power Envelope (OVTASK-143):** the power envelope bounds the power reference the speed-power loop can command: power headroom and rates change the loop behaviour at the limits.
risk: Too soft: speed deviations from the optimal tip-speed ratio (AEP loss), slow RSA window crossing. Too aggressive: torque fluctuations, drivetrain fatigue, grid flicker, interaction with ADTD2.

tasks.name: Speed-Power Controller: Gain Scheduling
scope: Schedules the gains of the speed-power PI over the operating range (rotor speed / power), because the sensitivity of the aerodynamic torque to rotor speed changes strongly between cut-in and rated.
Goal: uniform speed-loop dynamics and stability margin in the whole partial-load region.
kpi: - Stability margin and closed-loop bandwidth of the speed-power loop at several operating points.
- Speed tracking and torque activity per wind bin (DLC 1.2a).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a over the whole partial-load range (each wind bin is a different operating point of the schedule).
**Medium:** DLC 3.x start-up (low-speed end of the schedule).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Power Controller (PI) (OVTASK-159):** the gain schedule sets the effective loop gain of the speed-power PI over the partial-load speed range: changing it changes the loop margins at every speed.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Speed-Power Controller (PI) (OVTASK-159):** the gain schedule is relative to the speed-power PI gains: changing Kp changes the gain at every scheduled speed.
risk: Schedule not matched to the rotor: too high gain at some operating points (torque oscillations, drivetrain fatigue) or too low (poor tracking, AEP loss).

tasks.name: Resonance Speed Avoider (RSA)
scope: Keeps the rotor speed out of resonance windows (rotor 1P / 3P crossing tower frequencies, other configured windows): the speed reference jumps across the window and the speed-power / speed-pitch controllers are scheduled so that the rotor spends little time inside it.
Windows are defined by the Resonance Speed Window Configuration (centre, limits, power limits, switching times).
kpi: - Time spent inside the windows and tower fatigue / nacelle acceleration at the tower frequency (DLC 1.2a around the window speed).
- Number of window crossings and power / AEP loss.
- Stability of the crossing (no hunting at the window edges).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a at the wind speeds where the rotor would run inside the window (3P crossing the tower 1st mode drives tower fatigue).
**Medium:** DLC 3.x start-up and DLC 4.x shut-down (crossing the window while accelerating / decelerating); DLC 1.3 ETM.
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Power Trajectory: Speed-Power Curve (OVTASK-308):** the speed window avoided by RSA lies on the curve: the power levels at the window edges, and so the time to cross the window, depend on the curve.

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** RSA moves the speed-pitch reference and loop gain to cross the resonance window; its activation and mode-switch times (RSA_SpdPitCtrlActivationTime, RSA_TimePitModeSwitch) assume the speed-loop response, so they must be re-checked when the loop changes.

- **Speed-Power Controller (PI) (OVTASK-159):** in partial load the speed-power loop crosses the RSA window: its bandwidth and power rate limits set the crossing time and the power drop RSA_MinPwrReq must allow.
risk: Window missing or misplaced: operation at tower resonance, high tower fatigue and vibrations. Too wide or too slow crossings: AEP loss and speed / power transients.

tasks.name: Grid Fault Ride Through (GFRT)
scope: Handles the controller side of grid voltage faults the converter rides through: it latches the pre-fault speed and power, sets the power reference and ramps during and after the fault (recovery, post-fault), scales the speed-pitch gains and feed-forward against overspeed, and scales the drivetrain and tower dampers.
Goal: keep the turbine connected and within speed and load limits during and after the dip, and recover power as the grid code requires.
kpi: - Rotor speed peak and margin to the overspeed monitors during and after the dip (DLC 2.5a LVRT, DLC 2.1g).
- Power recovery time and ramp vs grid-code requirements.
- Drivetrain torque and tower loads during the dip and the recovery (dampers scaled).
- Correct handling of repeated faults.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.5a LVRT (voltage dip: torque drops, the rotor accelerates, then power must recover); DLC 2.1g grid drop (complete loss of torque).
**Medium:** DLC 2.3 EOG with grid drop (gust and torque loss together).
**Lower:** DLC 1.2a (no fault: GFRT must stay inactive).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the speed-pitch gain scaling during and after a grid fault (GFRT_Post_*SpdPit*) changes the effective loop gain the PI was tuned for, and so the speed recovery after the fault.
- **Speed-Pitch Controller: Feed-Forward (OVTASK-113):** the grid-fault feed-forward is triggered and timed by the ride-through states (GFRT_*): the feed-forward gains are set for that timing.

- **Active Drive Train Damper 2 (ADTD2) (OVTASK-292):** the post-fault power recovery (GFRT_Post_* power limits and ramps) decides how much the drivetrain mode is excited after a grid fault, and so how much the drivetrain damper must act.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** after a grid fault the speed loop must stop the acceleration: the post-fault gain reduction and its time window (GFRT_Post_*SpdPit*) scale the tuned PI gains.

- **Active Drive Train Damper 2 (ADTD2) (OVTASK-292):** a grid fault excites the drivetrain mode; the damper gain during and after the fault (ADTD2_GainFactGFRT, GFRT_Post_ADTD2AccThres) and the post-fault power ramps are tuned together.
risk: Poor fault handling: overspeed alarms or safety trips after grid dips, high drivetrain and tower loads, slow or oscillating power recovery (grid-code non-compliance).
The function depends on the converter topology: a full converter allows the inherited behaviour; a different topology means re-tuning from scratch.

tasks.name: Tower Vibration Monitor
scope: Prevents the tower from reaching critical loads: it monitors the fore-aft and side-side nacelle accelerations (slow and fast vibration levels) and stops the turbine when the limits are exceeded.
Event details (operating state, pitch, speed, wind, yaw error) are logged with each alarm.
kpi: - Margin between the vibration limits and the accelerations reached in normal and extreme operation (no nuisance stops).
- Detection of abnormal tower vibration (e.g. resonance, loss of damping) before critical loads.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a / 1.3 (highest normal and extreme-turbulence vibration levels: margin to the limits); DLC 2.x with stops and DLC 4.2 / 5.1 (tower swing after a stop).
**Medium:** operation near the tower resonance (RSA windows), DLC 2.4 yaw error.
**Lower:** DLC 6.x idling (side-side vibration in parked conditions).
affects: None to a high degree: its parameters only set alarm / stop limits; they do not change how other functions control the turbine (a wrong limit gives false or late stops, not a different tuning).
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the normal tower fore-aft acceleration level comes from the speed-loop response: the vibration limits must stay above it with margin.

- **Tower Acceleration Limiter (TAL) (OVTASK-139):** TAL limits the tower acceleration: the vibration-monitor limits must sit above the TAL activation levels so that TAL acts before the monitor stops the turbine.
risk: Limits too low: nuisance stops and availability loss. Too high: the tower can reach critical loads without protection.

tasks.name: Operation with Ice (OWI)
scope: Handles operation in icing conditions, either for maximum production or for personal safety: depending on the selected type (OpWIceTy) it stops the turbine or keeps it running with adapted operation (pitch offset, speed / power limits, de-icing support, idling start-up).
Implemented in the legacy STC1 controller; the PLANC model contains a helper that emulates its outputs.
kpi: - Power production in iced conditions vs the iced power curve.
- Loads with ice (DLC 1.7 OWI, DLC 6.4o / 7.1o idling with ice) within the design.
- Correct switching between modes and with the ice detection.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.7 OWI (power production with iced blades: mass imbalance and changed aerodynamics); DLC 6.4o and 7.1o idling with ice.
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Low Power Detector (OVTASK-278):** operation with ice lowers the power curve on purpose (de-icing / anti-icing modes): the low-power thresholds per mode (LPDC_OWI_*, LPDC_AntiIce_*) are set for that power loss.

- **Rotor Performance Monitor (OVTASK-286):** operation with ice lowers the power curve on purpose (de-icing / anti-icing modes): the wind speed error accepted per ice mode (RotPerfM_WindSpdError*Ice*) follows the performance loss of the iced rotor in each mode.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Wrong pitch offset or limits: loads above design with iced blades or unnecessary production loss. Wrong mode handling: running when a stop is required for safety.

tasks.name: Flex Configuration
scope: Defines the power concept of the turbine: design power (the rating the turbine is designed and certified for) and rated power (the power it is operated at, flexible below the design power), and provides them as active limits.
Implemented in the legacy STC1 controller; ActLimit_PwDesign / ActLimit_PwRated are inputs of many functions.
kpi: - Design and rated power consistent with the confirmed rating, the power envelope and the certification.
- All functions normalised with the design power behave correctly at the selected rated power.
dlcs: **High:** power-curve runs and DLC 1.2a (rated power sets the operating point above rated).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Power Trajectory: Speed-Power Curve (OVTASK-308):** the rated power (PwrDesign) is the end point of the speed-power curve.
- **Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch Curve (OVTASK-140):** the rated power sets where the opti-pitch curve ends and pitch regulation starts.
- **Speed-Pitch Controller: Aerodynamic Gain Scheduling (OVTASK-125):** the rated point (power and speed) is where the speed-pitch loop starts; the gain schedule is built from there to cut-out.
- **Power Boost (OVTASK-141):** boost levels and conditions are defined relative to the rated power and speed.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Wrong design or rated power: every normalised function is off-scale (limits, gains, detections) and the turbine operates outside its certified rating.

tasks.name: Pitch Control States: General Pitch Rate Limits
scope: Defines how the pitch is controlled in each operating state (speed regulation, waiting for rpm, active idle, stop, pitch to start, off) and the general pitch-rate limits: maximum positive / negative pitch-reference rates, with adjustments for load reduction (TAL gain), torque mismatch and stop zones.
These rate limits bound how fast every pitch-based function can act.
kpi: - Pitch-rate limits consistent with the pitch-system capability and the blade / tower loads in stops.
- Speed control not saturated by the rate limits in gusts and grid faults (overspeed peaks).
- Correct state transitions (start-up, stop, idle) without pitch steps.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 4.x / 5.1 shut-downs and DLC 2.x faults with stop (pitch-out rate sets tower and blade loads and the stopping time); DLC 1.4 / 2.1g (rate limit vs speed-loop demand).
**Medium:** DLC 3.x start-up (pitch to start, waiting for rpm).
**Lower:** DLC 1.2a (normal operation rarely at the limit).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the general pitch-rate limits (SpdPit_MaxPitRefRatePos / Neg) bound the pitch rate of the speed loop: when they are reached the loop saturates and speed peaks grow.
- **Tower Acceleration Limiter (TAL) (OVTASK-139):** TAL reduces the positive pitch-rate limit (SpdPit_MaxPitRefRatePosLoadRed): its effect is relative to the general limit.
- **Controller Overspeed Monitor (OVTASK-123):** the pitch rates in stops and at high speed error set how fast the rotor is braked aerodynamically, and so the overspeed peaks the limits must accept.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Limits too high: pitch-system overload and high tower / blade loads in stops. Too low: speed control saturated, overspeed in gusts and faults, slow stops.

tasks.name: Speed-Pitch Controller: Aerodynamic Gain Scheduling
scope: Schedules the speed-pitch PI gains with the pitch angle, rotor speed and estimated wind speed, compensating the strong change of the aerodynamic sensitivity (dP/dpitch) over the full-load range.
Goal: the same loop dynamics and stability margin from rated to cut-out.
kpi: - Stability margin and bandwidth of the speed-pitch loop at operating points from rated to cut-out.
- Rotor-speed std / max and pitch activity per wind bin above rated (DLC 1.2a).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a above rated (each wind bin is a different operating point of the schedule); DLC 1.4 / 9.4c (fast movement through the schedule during a gust).
**Medium:** DLC 1.3 ETM; high-wind operation with HWO (curtailed operating points).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the PI is tuned at a reference operating point and the schedule extends it to the full-load range: a change of the schedule changes the loop gain and margins in the rest of the range, and the reverse.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Rotor Performance Data (OVTASK-345):** the aerodynamic sensitivity dP/dpitch that the gain schedule compensates comes from the same rotor aerodynamics: a new rotor or new tables require a new schedule.

- **Wind Speed Estimator (OVTASK-155):** the estimated wind speed is a breakpoint of the gain schedule: an estimate bias moves the scheduled gain away from the actual operating point, mainly near rated where the aerodynamic sensitivity changes fastest.
- **Flex Configuration (OVTASK-307):** the rated point (power and speed) is where the speed-pitch loop starts; the gain schedule is built from there to cut-out.
- **Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch Curve (OVTASK-140):** the pitch at rated is the first point of the gain schedule: the aerodynamic sensitivity at the start of full load depends on it.
- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the schedule is relative to the reference gains Kp / Ti: changing them changes the gain at every scheduled point.
- **High Wind Operator (HWO) (OVTASK-154):** the high-wind curtailment adds operating points (reduced speed and power at high pitch) that the gain schedule must cover with margin.
risk: Schedule not matched to the rotor: unstable or oscillating speed loop at some wind speeds, or sluggish response (overspeed peaks).

tasks.name: Speed-Pitch Controller: High Speed Gain
scope: Increases the speed-pitch gain when the rotor speed approaches the overspeed region (start offset above the reference, two gain levels), so that the pitch reacts harder only when overspeed is near.
Goal: lower overspeed peaks in extreme events without making normal operation more aggressive.
kpi: - Rotor-speed peaks and margin to the controller overspeed monitor in extreme gusts (DLC 9.4c, 1.4).
- No activation in normal operation (DLC 1.2a) and no pitch chatter when it engages.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 9.4c ECG frontal passage and DLC 1.4 ECD (sustained gusts drive the speed towards the overspeed limits).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Controller Overspeed Monitor (OVTASK-123):** the High Speed Gain (SpdPit_HSG_*) raises the loop gain near the speed limits: it sets the peak speed the overspeed limits have to accept.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Speed Limit by Collective Pitch (SLCP) (OVTASK-165):** the speed limited by the collective pitch (flutter boundary) moves the speed limit near which the High Speed Gain acts.
risk: Too weak or too late: overspeed stops in extreme gusts. Too strong or too early: pitch chatter and higher loads in normal operation.

tasks.name: Speed-Pitch Controller: Feed-Forward
scope: Adds a pitch feed-forward to the speed-pitch integrator from changes of the effective power reference (and from the pitch trip avoider), and a dedicated feed-forward during grid faults whose gain is scaled with the time to the active overspeed limit.
Goal: anticipate the aerodynamic torque change when the power reference or the generator torque changes quickly, instead of waiting for the speed error.
kpi: - Speed peak and recovery after power-reference steps (curtailment, boost, frequency response) and after grid faults.
- No overspeed alarms during LVRT / grid drop (DLC 2.5a, 2.1g).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.5a LVRT and DLC 2.1g grid drop (torque drops instantly: the feed-forward pitches before the speed rises).
**Medium:** power-reference steps (curtailment, park control, frequency response).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Controller Overspeed Monitor (OVTASK-123):** the pitch feed-forward on power-reference changes and grid faults (SpdPit_DeltaPwrToPitFFGain, SpdPit_GFRT_*FF) decides how much speed rise the faults cause: the overspeed limits must cover the remaining peaks.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Grid Fault Ride Through (GFRT) (OVTASK-301):** the grid-fault feed-forward is triggered and timed by the ride-through states (GFRT_*): the feed-forward gains are set for that timing.
risk: Too little: overspeed peaks and alarms after grid faults and fast curtailments. Too much: over-pitching, power dips and speed undershoot.

tasks.name: Speed Limit by Collective Pitch (SLCP)
scope: Curtails the rotor speed as a function of the collective pitch reference, to keep the blades away from the flutter boundary (speed vs pitch) given by Loads.
Outputs a speed limit to the Reduction Interface (with compensation for the RSA windows).
kpi: - Margin of the operating trajectory (speed vs pitch) to the flutter boundary in all operating cases.
- AEP / speed loss caused by the curtailment.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a and DLC 1.3 at high wind (high pitch and speed together: closest to the flutter boundary); DLC 1.4 / 9.4 (speed peaks at high pitch).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Speed-Pitch Controller: High Speed Gain (OVTASK-124):** the speed limited by the collective pitch (flutter boundary) moves the speed limit near which the High Speed Gain acts.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Missing or too high: operation close to blade flutter (aeroelastic instability, safety). Too conservative: AEP loss at high wind.

tasks.name: Reduction Interface
scope: Consolidates every reduction of power and speed (ACS, HWO, SLCP, SLP, safe mode, vibration monitors, frequency control, park pilot, HTRT, idle, boost...) into the active references and limits (ActRef.Power / Speed, ActLimit.*) used by the speed controllers, with minimum speed / power references and local limits.
Implemented in the legacy STC1 controller (emulated in the PLANC model).
kpi: - Correct minimum selection and priority of the reduction sources; smooth transitions between them.
- Minimum speed references (idle, cut-in) consistent with the RSA windows and the speed-power curve.
dlcs: **High:** curtailed operation (DLC 9.7 curtailed operation, derated cases) and high-wind operation with HWO.
**Medium:** DLC 1.3 with ACS active; start-up (cut-in speed).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch at Curtailed Speed (OPCS) (OVTASK-157):** the local power / speed limits (LocalPwrLimOEM, LocalRotSpdLimOEM) define the curtailed operating points for which the curtailed opti-pitch is designed.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Wrong priority or limits: the turbine follows the wrong reduction (loads above design or unnecessary AEP loss), reference steps, minimum speed inside a resonance window.

tasks.name: Speed Limit by Power (SLP)
scope: Reduces the speed reference during derated power operation, using the power envelope and the aerodynamic tables: when the power is limited, running at full speed would only add loads and noise, and the speed loop would work with a larger margin to overspeed.
Outputs a speed limit to the Reduction Interface.
kpi: - Speed vs power in derated operation along the inverse power envelope.
- Loads in derated operation (blade, tower, DLC 1.4 at derated power) and smooth derate / release transitions.
- [P] AEP impact when the park derates.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 9.7 curtailed operation with ECD (gust while derated: speed peak and loads depend on the reduced speed reference); derated-power operation cases.
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Wind Speed Estimator (OVTASK-155):** the speed limit table (SLP_RotSpdTbl) is indexed with the estimated wind speed.
- **Power Trajectory: Speed-Power Curve (OVTASK-308):** the speed limited by power is a cut of the speed-power curve.
risk: Speed not reduced: higher loads and overspeed risk in derated operation. Reduced too much: unstable or inefficient operation, speed / power transients at derate and release.

tasks.name: Controller Safe Mode
scope: Defines the fallback operation when a load handle is not available (IPC, PDA, BLL, GILL, TTCC status not OK, blade-load or azimuth sensors invalid): power / speed derating or degradation, pitch tables and boost disable, so that the loads stay within the design without that load handle.
Outputs the safe-mode reductions to the Reduction Interface / ACS and a safe-mode pitch table.
kpi: - Loads in safe mode (each load handle disabled) within the design with the derating applied.
- AEP / availability cost of the safe mode; correct entry and exit conditions.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.1i / 2.4i blade-sensor failure and replication cases (load handles lose their input and the turbine must run in safe mode).
**Medium:** DLC 1.2a / 1.3 with load handles disabled (fatigue and extremes in derated operation).
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Individual Pitch Control (IPC) (OVTASK-133):** the safe-mode derating when IPC is unavailable (SafeMode_IPC_*) must compensate the load reduction the tuned IPC gives.
- **Blade Load Limiter (BLL) (OVTASK-127):** the safe-mode derating when BLL / GILL are unavailable (SafeMode_BLLandGILL_*) must compensate their load reduction.
- **Gust Induced Load Limiter (GILL) (OVTASK-130):** the safe-mode derating when BLL / GILL are unavailable (SafeMode_BLLandGILL_*) must compensate the load reduction the tuned GILL gives.
risk: Derating too small: loads above design while a load handle is missing. Too large: availability and AEP loss on every sensor fault.

tasks.name: Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch at Curtailed Speed (OPCS)
scope: Adapts the minimum pitch when the rotor speed is curtailed below nominal (speed reduction by ACS, HWO, SLP, RSA, curtailment): at a lower speed the optimal pitch for a given power is different, and keeping the nominal opti-pitch would lose efficiency or raise loads.
The curtailed-speed pitch curve is read from the active speed-power curve and the active speed reference.
kpi: - Aerodynamic efficiency / power in curtailed-speed operation.
- Loads (thrust, flap) in curtailed operation and smooth activation / deactivation.
dlcs: **High:** curtailed-speed operation (DLC 9.7 curtailed operation, ACS / HWO curtailment cases).
**Medium:** DLC 1.3 with ACS active (speed curtailed by ACS).
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch Curve (OVTASK-140):** the curtailed opti-pitch is derived from the same pitch tables; both must be consistent at the transition.
- **Reduction Interface (OVTASK-156):** the local power / speed limits (LocalPwrLimOEM, LocalRotSpdLimOEM) define the curtailed operating points for which the curtailed opti-pitch is designed.
risk: Wrong curtailed curve: AEP loss or higher thrust / flap loads whenever the speed is curtailed.

tasks.name: Pitch Trajectory Offsets: Optimal Start Angle (OptiStart)
scope: Computes the pitch offset used when the turbine starts (optimal start angle) as a function of the lead-filtered rotor speed and the cut-out speed, so that the rotor accelerates to cut-in quickly without large aerodynamic loads.
Part of the minimum-pitch calculation of Pitch Trajectory Offsets.
kpi: - Start-up time to cut-in and loads during the run-up (DLC 3.1 / 3.2 / 3.3).
- No overspeed or pitch oscillation at the transition to speed control.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 3.1 NWP start-up, DLC 3.2 EOG and DLC 3.3 EDC start-up (gust or direction change while the rotor runs up).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Operation (state machine) (OVTASK-328):** the start pitch angle and the kick-start speeds of the operation state machine together define the aerodynamic torque and the time to reach the connection speed at start-up.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Start angle too low: high loads and possible overspeed during the run-up. Too high: slow or failed start-ups in low wind (availability).

tasks.name: Speed Control Scheduler: Full Power State Machine
scope: Schedules which speed controller is active: speed-power in regions 1-2, speed-pitch in region 3. The full power state machine (FPSM) decides the transition using the regulated power, the pitch gap to the minimum pitch and the speed error, and builds the speed references of both controllers (with external offsets).
Goal: smooth, unambiguous switching between power and pitch control around rated.
kpi: - Smooth transitions at rated (no power dips, speed peaks or limit cycling between the controllers) in DLC 1.2a around rated wind.
- Power-curve / AEP around rated.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a at wind speeds around rated (continuous switching between regions in turbulence).
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Pitch Trajectory Offsets: Pitch Limit by Wind (PLBW) (OVTASK-138):** the gap to the minimum pitch (FPSM_*_PitGapToMinPit) that decides the full-power state is measured from this minimum pitch.

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the pitch fluctuations around the minimum pitch near rated, set by the loop, decide whether the full-power state toggles: the gap to minimum pitch and the times (FPSM_*) are set for them.
- **Power Boost (OVTASK-141):** the full-power state uses gaps to minimum pitch per boost type (FPSM_BoostTyp*_PitGapToMinPit): they are set for the boost pitch offsets.
risk: Wrong thresholds: hunting between the two controllers, power dips and speed peaks around rated, higher drivetrain and tower fatigue.

tasks.name: Operation (state machine)
scope: State machine that starts, operates and stops the turbine: start-up sequence, cut-in / cut-out conditions (rotor speed, wind), stop types and stop-ramp selection, idling and kick-start requests.
Implemented in the legacy STC1 controller (emulated in the PLANC model). The WTGType parameters are the start / stop speeds and wind thresholds.
kpi: - Start-up and stop sequences complete without overspeed or abnormal loads (DLC 3.x, 4.x, 5.1).
- Cut-out / restart thresholds at high wind consistent with HWO and the loads.
- Availability: no unnecessary stops or failed start-ups.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 3.1-3.3 start-up and DLC 4.1-4.2 / 5.1 shut-downs (sequence and timing set the transient loads).
**Medium:** DLC 6.x idling (transition to idle) and high-wind cut-out.
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Power Control States (OVTASK-330):** the cut-out speed and stop conditions (CutOut_RotSpd) and the stop power ramps (CutOut_*) act in the same stop: the ramp time must suit the speed at which the stop starts.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Pitch Trajectory Offsets: Optimal Start Angle (OptiStart) (OVTASK-116):** the start pitch angle and the kick-start speeds of the operation state machine together define the aerodynamic torque and the time to reach the connection speed at start-up.
risk: Wrong start / stop speeds: failed start-ups, overspeed in start-up, harsh stops (loads) or stops at the wrong wind speed (AEP).

tasks.name: Inertial Response (IR)
scope: Provides additional active power during an under-frequency event of the grid (park-level function): the turbine releases rotational kinetic energy for a short time, then recovers speed with a reduced power.
It estimates the available power and the speed drop it may accept, overrides the speed-power control and adds a pitch offset during the recovery.
kpi: - Extra power delivered and its duration vs the grid requirement.
- Rotor-speed drop and recovery (no stall, no stop, no under-speed) and loads during the event.
dlcs: **High:** inertial-response events at different wind speeds (power boost from kinetic energy and recovery).
**Medium:** events at low wind (small kinetic energy: risk of under-speed).
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Rotor Performance Data (OVTASK-345):** the power that can be extracted during and after the inertial response is computed from the rotor power table.
risk: Too much energy taken: deep speed drop, stall or stop, high loads in the recovery. Too little: grid requirement not met.

tasks.name: Power Control States
scope: Defines how the power is controlled in each operating scenario: efficiency regulation on / off, stop ramps (as a function of time, speed or torque), ramp to active idling, effective power-reference change and the regulated power reference sent to the converter.
The stop ramp sets how fast the generator power is removed when the turbine stops.
kpi: - Drivetrain torque and tower loads during stop ramps (DLC 4.x, 5.1).
- Power reference continuity (no steps) and correct effective power-reference change for the pitch feed-forward.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 4.1 / 4.2 shut-downs and DLC 5.1 emergency stop (power ramp-down vs pitch-out sets drivetrain and tower transients).
**Medium:** grid events (power reference latched in GFRT).
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Operation (state machine) (OVTASK-328):** the cut-out speed and stop conditions (CutOut_RotSpd) and the stop power ramps (CutOut_*) act in the same stop: the ramp time must suit the speed at which the stop starts.
risk: Stop ramps too fast: drivetrain torque reversal and tower loads; too slow: overspeed during the stop. Wrong effective power change: wrong feed-forward to the pitch.

tasks.name: Speed Control Scheduler: Speed Shifter
scope: Shifts the speed references of the speed-power and speed-pitch controllers (SpdRefHa.PwrSpeed / PitSpeed) apart around rated, with ramp rates depending on power and pitch changes, so that the two controllers do not fight each other and the transition between regions is smooth.
External offsets (LIDAR, rotor sync, floater motion) are added here.
kpi: - Speed tracking and controller transitions around rated (DLC 1.2a).
- No limit cycling between speed-power and speed-pitch; pitch activity at rated.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a around rated wind (where the speed shift acts continuously in turbulence).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the speed shift between the pitch and power speed references (SpdShift_*) sets how far the rotor speed must rise before pitch acts: it changes the speed excursions around rated.

- **Speed-Power Controller (PI) (OVTASK-159):** the speed shift between the pitch and power speed references (SpdShift_*) decides at which speed torque stops increasing and pitch takes over: it changes the speed-power loop behaviour near rated.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Shift too small: the two controllers interact (power and pitch oscillations around rated). Too large: speed deviations and AEP loss, overspeed margin reduced.

tasks.name: Controller Functionality Scheduler
scope: Coordinates the load handles: priorities between BLL and PDA, GILL and PDA, TTCC and PDA, IPC / PDA activation, allowed IPC and TTCC amplitudes, and sums the individual pitch offsets (IPC, TTCC, PDA) into the per-blade pitch commands.
Goal: the load handles act together without compounding or cancelling each other.
kpi: - Loads with all load handles active vs each handle alone (no compounded pitch-out, no loss of protection).
- Pitch bearing damage and AEP with the chosen priorities.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a / 1.2c (IPC, PDA and TTCC active together: fatigue and clearance); DLC 1.4 and gust cases (GILL / BLL vs PDA priority).
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Individual Pitch Control (IPC) (OVTASK-133):** the IPC pitch amplitudes allowed per state (FuncSche_IPCAllowedPitAmp*) are set from the amplitude the tuned IPC needs.
- **Tip to Tower Clearance Controller (TTCC) (OVTASK-128):** the maximum TTCC offset (TTCC_PitOffsetMax) in the scheduler bounds the TTCC action.
- **Blade Load Limiter (BLL) (OVTASK-127):** the priority between BLL and PDA (FuncSche_BLLPDA_PrioritizationMode) decides which pitch offset wins when both act.
