- **Gust Induced Load Limiter (GILL) (OVTASK-130):** the priority between GILL and PDA (FuncSche_GILLPDA_PrioritizationMode) decides which pitch offset wins when both act.

- **Pitch Damage Attenuator (PDA) (OVTASK-136):** the PDA activation level in operation (FuncSche_PDAActivationLevelOperat) and its priority against BLL / GILL depend on how much pitch travel PDA removes.
risk: Wrong priorities: compounded pitch-out (AEP loss, overspeed), or PDA cancelling a protective action (extremes, clearance).

tasks.name: Active Tower Damper Side-Side (ATD)
scope: Reduces the tower-base side-side loads by superimposing a damping signal on the power (generator torque) reference: the side-side nacelle acceleration is band-pass filtered around the tower 1st / 2nd modes, phase-shifted and turned into a power oscillation that damps the tower side-side motion.
Gain scheduled with rotor speed and power; amplitude limited by the power envelope.
kpi: - Tower-base side-side fatigue (DEL) and damping of the side-side mode (DLC 1.2a, misaligned / low-turbulence cases).
- Power oscillation amplitude and its use of the power envelope; no excitation of drivetrain modes.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a (side-side fatigue, especially at low turbulence where aerodynamic damping side-side is low).
**Medium:** DLC 6.x idling (no torque available: ATD inactive) and grid faults (scaled).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Dynamic Power Envelope (OVTASK-143):** the power envelope reserves headroom for the damping power of the side-side tower damper (ATD_X_MaxPwr and the ATD power estimate in the envelope): the reserve is sized from the power the tuned damper needs.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Wrong phase or gain: no damping or negative damping of the side-side mode (tower fatigue up); too much power oscillation: drivetrain loads, flicker.

tasks.name: Pitch Reference Limiter
scope: Keeps each blade pitch reference within the minimum / maximum limits of the pitch system and limits its rate, with a dead-band; combines the collective reference with the individual offsets (service mode).
It is the last stage before the pitch servo: its rate limit bounds every pitch action.
kpi: - Rate-limit occupancy of the blade references in gusts, grid faults and stops.
- No overspeed or load increase caused by the limit; references always within the mechanical limits.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.4 / 9.4 gusts and DLC 2.1g / 2.5a (largest pitch-rate demand of the speed loop).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the maximum pitch-reference rate and deadband (SpdPit_PitRefMaxRate, PitRefDeadband) bound what the speed loop can command: a rate limit hit in gusts or grid faults saturates the loop (larger speed peaks); the deadband reduces pitch activity but adds a dead zone in the loop.
- **Individual Pitch Control (IPC) (OVTASK-133):** the same rate limit applies to collective plus cyclic pitch: it bounds the IPC amplitude that can be added at high collective activity.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Rate limit too low: speed loop and load handles saturated (overspeed, higher loads). Too high: pitch-system overload.

tasks.name: Power Trajectory: Speed-Power Curve
scope: Defines the power as a function of rotor speed (speed-power curve) that maximises the power extracted by the rotor in partial load, i.e. the optimal tip-speed-ratio trajectory, and the transition to rated.
It is the reference the speed-power controller follows; the active curve is also read by OPCS, RSA and the power estimator.
kpi: - Power curve / AEP in partial load (optimal tip-speed ratio).
- Loads and noise along the curve (rotor speed in partial load).
dlcs: **High:** power-curve runs and DLC 1.2a in partial load (AEP).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Power Controller (PI) (OVTASK-159):** the speed-power curve is the trajectory the speed-power loop follows in partial load: its slope sets the loop gain needed and the torque the drivetrain sees.

- **Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch Curve (OVTASK-140):** the curve sets the tip-speed ratio at each wind speed, and the optimal pitch is defined for that tip-speed ratio: curve and opti-pitch are designed together.
- **Power Trajectory: Scaling of the Speed-Power Curve during Start-Up (OVTASK-115):** the scaling of the speed-power curve at start-up is applied to this curve.
- **Resonance Speed Avoider (RSA) (OVTASK-162):** the speed window avoided by RSA lies on the curve: the power levels at the window edges, and so the time to cross the window, depend on the curve.
- **Speed Limit by Power (SLP) (OVTASK-112):** the speed limited by power is a cut of the speed-power curve.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Flex Configuration (OVTASK-307):** the rated power (PwrDesign) is the end point of the speed-power curve.
risk: Sub-optimal curve: AEP loss; too high speeds in partial load: noise and loads.

tasks.name: Power Trajectory: Scaling of the Speed-Power Curve during Start-Up
scope: Scales the speed-power curve during the start-up (after cut-in) so that power is taken gradually while the rotor reaches its operating speed, with a time limit for the scaling.
Goal: a smooth start without speed undershoot or torque steps.
kpi: - Start-up time and smoothness (no speed dip, no torque step) in DLC 3.x.
- Drivetrain torque during the start-up.
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Power Trajectory: Speed-Power Curve (OVTASK-308):** the scaling of the speed-power curve at start-up is applied to this curve.
risk: Wrong scaling: slow start-ups (availability), speed undershoot or torque transients at cut-in.

tasks.name: Tower Frequency Monitor
scope: Detects structural changes of the turbine (foundation, tower, bolted joints) through a drift of the estimated tower frequency from its calibrated value, and shuts the turbine down for inspection.
Calibration is reset when the tower frequency estimator is reset.
kpi: - Normal frequency scatter (temperature, mass of ice, operating point) vs the alarm threshold: no false alarms.
- Detection of a frequency drift that indicates a structural change.
dlcs: **High:** operation over the whole wind range (DLC 1.2a: natural variation of the estimated tower frequency).
**Medium:** DLC 1.7 OWI (ice mass lowers the frequency).
affects: None to a high degree: its parameters only set alarm / stop limits; they do not change how other functions control the turbine (a wrong limit gives false or late stops, not a different tuning).
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Threshold too tight: false stops. Too loose: structural damage not detected.

tasks.name: Rotor Sensor Fusion (RSF)
scope: Fuses the independent rotor-speed and azimuth measurements (hub, main-shaft, generator, converter, safety-system sensors) into high-quality rotor speed, acceleration and direction estimates, using their validation status.
The enable mask selects which sources are fused.
kpi: - Accuracy and noise of the fused speed / acceleration vs the true rotor speed; correct handling of failed sources.
- Correct rotation-direction detection.
dlcs: **High:** sensor-failure cases (DLC 2.1i and speed-sensor faults: fusion must reject the failed source).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Speed Mismatch Monitor (OVTASK-336):** the fused speed and the source mask (RSF_*) define which deviation between sensors is normal, which sets the mismatch limits.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Wrong fusion or mask: noisy or biased rotor speed / acceleration in all speed-based functions, wrong reaction to a failed sensor.

tasks.name: Yaw Misalignment Monitor (YMM)
scope: Monitors the measured misalignment between nacelle and wind direction against allowable limits that depend on wind speed; on large misalignment it adds a pitch offset (load protection) and informs the yaw offset interface.
Goal: protect the rotor from the loads of large yaw errors (e.g. wind-vane faults, yaw-system problems).
kpi: - Loads with large yaw misalignment (DLC 2.4a/b) with the monitor active.
- No activation in normal yaw tracking (DLC 1.2a); AEP cost of the pitch offset.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.4a/b extreme yaw error (the case the monitor protects against).
**Medium:** DLC 1.2a (normal yaw errors must not trigger it).
affects: None to a high degree: its parameters only set alarm / stop limits; they do not change how other functions control the turbine (a wrong limit gives false or late stops, not a different tuning).
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Limits too loose: high blade and hub loads with large yaw error. Too tight: unnecessary pitch offsets (AEP).

tasks.name: Air Density
scope: Computes the local air density (from temperature and pressure / altitude) and its ratio to the standard density, used to compensate power curves, pitch curves, wind and thrust estimates and detections.
Implemented in the legacy STC1 controller (emulated in the PLANC model).
kpi: - Density ratio vs the site density; correct fallback when the sensors fail.
- Consistency of the compensated estimates (wind, thrust, power curve) at low and high density.
dlcs: **High:** power-curve runs at non-standard density (compensation of opti-pitch and power curve).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Wind Speed Estimator (OVTASK-155):** the aerodynamic power scales with air density: the density used in the inversion of the power table sets the bias of the wind speed estimate.

- **Pitch Trajectory Tables: Opti-Pitch Curve (OVTASK-140):** the opti-pitch curve and its air-density compensation depend on the density: the optimum pitch and the thrust at a given wind speed change with it.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Wrong density: biased wind and thrust estimates, wrong opti-pitch at low density (AEP or loads), false low-power detections.

tasks.name: Low Power Detector
scope: Detects when the production deviates from the running power curve (degraded performance, ice on the blades), with density and yaw-misalignment compensation and several detection curves (general, ice, anti-ice, de-ice).
Feeds ice handling and performance alarms.
kpi: - No false detections in normal operation (scatter of power vs the detection curve, DLC 1.2a).
- Detection of the power loss caused by ice (DLC 1.7) within the required time.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.7 OWI (iced rotor: the power loss to detect); DLC 1.2a (normal scatter: false alarms).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Ice Detector (OVTASK-277):** aerodynamic ice detection uses the low-power detection: its threshold sets how early ice is detected.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Power Estimator (OVTASK-142):** the low-power detection compares the produced power with a percentage of the expected power: the margin (LPDC_*PercentOfPwrCrv) must cover the error of the expected power.

- **Operation with Ice (OWI) (OVTASK-158):** operation with ice lowers the power curve on purpose (de-icing / anti-icing modes): the low-power thresholds per mode (LPDC_OWI_*, LPDC_AntiIce_*) are set for that power loss.
risk: Too sensitive: false ice / performance stops. Too insensitive: iced operation not detected (ice throw risk, loads).

tasks.name: Rotor Azimuth Estimator and Monitor
scope: Estimates the rotor azimuth from the available sources (hub orientation / accelerometers, speed integration) with source selection, calibration and phase correction, and monitors its validity.
The azimuth is needed by every 1P / per-blade function (IPC, TTCC, blade monitors).
kpi: - Azimuth error vs the true azimuth over the speed range (phase error at 1P).
- Correct source switching and status when a source fails.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a (azimuth accuracy for IPC and TTCC timing).
**Medium:** start-up / low speed (estimation at low rotor speed).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Individual Pitch Control (IPC) (OVTASK-133):** IPC transforms the blade moments to tilt / yaw and back with the rotor azimuth: an azimuth offset or delay rotates the tilt / yaw axes, so the IPC gain and phase are only valid for a correct azimuth.

tasks.name: Active Drive Train Damper (ADTD, legacy)

tasks.name: Wind Speed Monitor

tasks.name: Active Power Regulation

tasks.name: Rotor Performance Data

kpi: - Tables consistent with the aerodynamic model of the final blade (power and thrust per operating point).
- Estimators unbiased when fed with these tables (DLC 1.2a).

**Medium:** DLC 1.7 OWI (iced rotor deviates from the tables).

- **Wind Speed Estimator (OVTASK-155):** the estimator inverts the rotor power table (RotPerfData_PwrTbl): any error of the aerodynamic table becomes a bias of the estimated wind speed over the whole range.
- **Thrust Estimator (OVTASK-153):** the thrust estimate is read from the rotor thrust table (RotPerfData_ThrustTbl, ThrustNom).

tasks.name: Ice Detector

- **Low Power Detector (OVTASK-278):** aerodynamic ice detection uses the low-power detection: its threshold sets how early ice is detected.

tasks.name: No Cut In Detector

- **Ice Detector (OVTASK-277):** the no-cut-in decision with ice uses the ice detector status: its sensitivity decides when the turbine may not start.

tasks.name: Blade Edge Frequency Monitor

affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.

affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.

tasks.name: Power Inflow Estimator

kpi: - Power-inflow estimate vs the aerodynamic power of the simulation, especially during speed transients.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a and DLC 1.4 (speed transients where electrical power differs from aerodynamic power).
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.

tasks.name: Speed Measurement Validator

kpi: - Correct detection of failed or implausible sources with no false invalidations.
affects: None to a high degree: its parameters only set alarm / stop limits; they do not change how other functions control the turbine (a wrong limit gives false or late stops, not a different tuning).
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.

tasks.name: Gearbox Slip Monitor
scope: Prevents the generator side and the rotor side of the drivetrain from slipping relative to each other (slip in the gearbox / shaft connection), which would introduce high loads, by comparing the two speeds / angles.
kpi: - Slip limit above the normal torsional deflection and measurement differences; detection of real slip.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.5a / 2.1g (large torque steps: largest torsional deflection).
affects: None to a high degree: its parameters only set alarm / stop limits; they do not change how other functions control the turbine (a wrong limit gives false or late stops, not a different tuning).
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Too tight: false stops after torque transients. Too loose: drivetrain damage not detected.

tasks.name: Rotor Performance Monitor
scope: Detects when the rotor does not perform as expected (wind-speed estimate vs measured wind, e.g. ice or blade degradation); currently in observer mode.
kpi: - Detection thresholds above the normal scatter between estimated and measured wind; detection of iced or degraded rotors.
affects: None to a high degree: its parameters only set alarm / stop limits; they do not change how other functions control the turbine (a wrong limit gives false or late stops, not a different tuning).
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Wind Speed Estimator (OVTASK-155):** the monitor compares the measured wind speed with the estimate: the normal error band (RotPerfM_WindSpdError*) depends on the accuracy of the estimator.

- **Operation with Ice (OWI) (OVTASK-158):** operation with ice lowers the power curve on purpose (de-icing / anti-icing modes): the wind speed error accepted per ice mode (RotPerfM_WindSpdError*Ice*) follows the performance loss of the iced rotor in each mode.

tasks.name: Speed Mismatch Monitor
scope: Identifies mismatches between the rotor-speed measurements of different sources (e.g. rotor vs generator speed through the gear ratio) and raises alarms, so that a faulty sensor or drivetrain problem is detected.
kpi: - Mismatch limits above normal differences (torsional dynamics, measurement noise) and below fault levels.
dlcs: **High:** speed-sensor failure cases and DLC 2.5a / 2.1g (torsional transients create apparent mismatch).
affects: None to a high degree: its parameters only set alarm / stop limits; they do not change how other functions control the turbine (a wrong limit gives false or late stops, not a different tuning).
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Speed Source Interface (OVTASK-97):** the mismatch limits (SpdMiMon_*) are set from the expected deviation between the selected speed sources.
- **Rotor Sensor Fusion (RSF) (OVTASK-96):** the fused speed and the source mask (RSF_*) define which deviation between sensors is normal, which sets the mismatch limits.
risk: Too tight: false alarms after transients. Too loose: faulty speed sensor not detected.

tasks.name: Blade Edgewise Vibration Monitor (BEVM)
scope: Prevents the blades from reaching a critical edgewise vibration level (fatigue or, in the worst case, edgewise instability): it band-pass filters the blade edge signals around the edgewise modes and, above the limits, adds a pitch offset, reduces the speed or stops the turbine.
kpi: - Vibration limits above the normal edgewise levels in operation and idling, and below critical levels.
- Effectiveness of the pitch offset / speed reduction on the edgewise vibration.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 6.x idling and parked with large yaw / inflow angles (edgewise vibration risk is highest in standstill and idling); DLC 1.7 OWI and 1.2a.
affects: None to a high degree: its parameters only set alarm / stop limits; they do not change how other functions control the turbine (a wrong limit gives false or late stops, not a different tuning).
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Too tight: unnecessary derating / stops. Too loose: edgewise vibrations not stopped (blade damage).

tasks.name: High Temperature Ride Through (HTRT)
scope: Extends the operational area at high ambient temperatures: instead of stopping when components get hot, the turbine is derated (power reduction) based on thermal models of the electrical components; it can also enable a speed boost in curtailment.
kpi: - Component temperatures within limits with the derating; production kept instead of stops at high temperature.
dlcs: **High:** high-temperature operation scenarios (not a load DLC; thermal cases).
affects: None to a high degree: changing its tunable parameters does not change the conditions for which other functions are tuned.
affected_by: None to a high degree: its tunable parameters are set from the turbine design and measurements, not from the tuning of other functions.
risk: Derating too late: component over-temperature and trips. Too early: AEP loss in hot climates.

tasks.name: Rotor Speed Filter
scope: Filters the measured rotor speed and rotor acceleration with a chain of band-stop (notch) filters at 3P, 6P, the 1st-3rd edgewise symmetric frequencies (1ES-3ES, centre frequencies estimated online by ESFE) and the tower 2nd mode (from the Tower Frequency Estimator), a generic band-stop, a low-pass and a lead filter.
Goal: remove the harmonic and structural content that would excite the control loops and the structure, without adding phase delay that degrades the speed control.
kpi: - Phase delay and gain of the filter chain (with and without lead filter) at the speed-loop crossover frequency.
- Attenuation of the rotor-speed spectrum at 3P, 6P, 1ES-3ES and the tower 2nd frequency, before vs after (DLC 1.2a).
- [P] Rotor speed std / max per wind bin (DLC 1.2a) and speed peak in gusts (DLC 1.4, 9.4w) not worse than the reference.
- [P] Pitch activity (RMS pitch rate) and fatigue of blade-root edgewise, pitch bearing, drivetrain and tower-base fore-aft in DLC 1.2a.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a normal turbulence (the rotor-speed spectrum carries 3P, edgewise and tower content; whatever passes the filters becomes pitch and torque activity and fatigue of pitch bearings, blades and drivetrain); DLC 1.4 ECD and DLC 9.4w extreme ECD with turbulence (the gust response of the speed loop depends on the phase of the filtered speed; ACS and the controller overspeed monitor are disabled, so the speed loop alone drives the tower and blade extremes).

**Medium:** DLC 2.1g grid drop and DLC 2.5a LVRT (torque is lost and the rotor accelerates fast: filter delay increases the speed peak seen by the speed-pitch loop and GFRT); DLC 1.3 ETM (large speed excursions in extreme turbulence).
**Lower:** DLC 1.2 NTM (baseline robustness); DLC 1.7 OWI (ice mass lowers the blade edgewise frequencies: the notches must follow the ESFE estimate).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the phase lag of the notch, low-pass and lead filters at the speed-loop crossover sets the phase margin left for the PI: changing the filters (1ES-3ES, 3P, 2T, lead) requires re-checking Kp and Ti.

- **Speed-Power Controller (PI) (OVTASK-159):** the phase lag of the speed filters at the crossover of the speed-power PI in partial load limits the gain that keeps a stability margin: changing the filters requires re-checking the PI gains.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Speed Source Interface (OVTASK-97):** the selected speed source (generator or rotor speed sensor) sets the resolution, noise and delay of the measured speed: the filter chain (low-pass, notches, lead) is dimensioned for that noise and delay.

- **Edgewise Synchronous Frequency Estimator (ESFE) (OVTASK-120):** the 1ES-3ES band-stop filters are centred on the ESFE estimates: the frequency range, initial frequency and threshold of ESFE decide whether the notches sit on the actual edgewise modes. A notch off the mode leaves edgewise content in the speed feedback and adds phase lag at the wrong frequency.
risk: **Band-stop filters (3P, 6P, 1ES-3ES, tower 2nd):** a mistuned notch lets harmonic or structural content into the pitch and power control: unintended pitch and power contributions, higher pitch bearing damage and excitation of blades, tower and drivetrain (fatigue, reduced lifetime). Too wide notches add phase delay to the speed loop.

**Low-pass filter:** too low a cut-off delays the speed response, reduces stability and can lead to overspeed; too high a cut-off leaves high-frequency content in the speed signal (pitch bearing damage, excitation of blades, tower and drivetrain).

**Lead filter:** too little lead gives delayed, less aggressive pitch reactions to gusts and higher extreme loads (DLC 1.4), especially without LOPC sensors; too much lead amplifies high-frequency content (pitch activity, fatigue).

tasks.name: Speed-Pitch Controller (PI)
scope: Controls the rotor speed with the collective pitch when the turbine is at rated power or at the active power reference: a PI controller with gain scheduling (pitch angle, rotor speed, wind speed) that tracks the speed-pitch set point SpdRefHa.PitSpeed = ActRef.Speed + SpeedShift_Pitch.

Includes a pitch feed-forward on effective power-reference changes, a feed-forward against overspeed during grid faults (gain scaled with the time to the overspeed limit) and a High Speed Gain near the speed limits. Its output PitchRefCollective is the base of every pitch command.
kpi: - Rotor speed mean, std and max per wind bin vs the active reference (DLC 1.2a).
- Overspeed peak (DLC 1.2a, 1.4) and time above the allowed high-speed region (flutter boundary).
- Tower-base fore-aft extreme in DLC 1.4.
- Constraints: pitch activity (RMS and max pitch rate, time at the pitch-rate limit), AEP, tower fore-aft fatigue in DLC 1.2a, no controller or safety overspeed alarm during grid faults (DLC 2.5).
- [P] Gain and phase margins of the linearised loop over the operating range.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a normal turbulence (speed regulation, pitch activity and tower fatigue); DLC 1.4 ECD (the speed peak and the tower fore-aft extreme in a gust depend on the loop bandwidth); DLC 2.5a LVRT and DLC 2.1g grid drop (generator torque is lost, so pitch is the only means to stop the acceleration); DLC 9.4c ECG frontal passage (a sustained gust pushes the speed towards the limits where the High Speed Gain acts).
**Medium:** DLC 1.3 ETM (large speed excursions); DLC 2.4a/b extreme yaw error (skewed inflow lowers the aerodynamic gain the scheduling assumes); DLC 2.1c controller overspeed.
**Lower:** DLC 1.2 NTM (robustness); DLC 1.7 OWI (iced blades change the aerodynamic gain).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Speed-Pitch Controller: Aerodynamic Gain Scheduling (OVTASK-125):** the schedule is relative to the reference gains Kp / Ti: changing them changes the gain at every scheduled point.

- **Speed-Power Controller (PI) (OVTASK-159):** near rated both loops are active around the transition: their bandwidths and the speed shift between their references decide whether they hand over smoothly or fight each other.

- **Blade Load Limiter (BLL) (OVTASK-127):** the extreme flapwise moments in gusts depend on how fast the speed loop pitches out: BLL thresholds and gain are set on the extremes left after the speed loop, so a new PI tuning requires re-checking BLL.

- **Gust Induced Load Limiter (GILL) (OVTASK-130):** the gust load left after the speed-loop response is what GILL has to remove: a new PI tuning changes the gust extremes and requires re-checking the GILL thresholds and gains.

- **Tower Acceleration Limiter (TAL) (OVTASK-139):** the tower fore-aft motion that TAL reacts to is driven by the thrust changes the speed loop makes: a faster loop excites or damps the tower 1st fore-aft mode differently, so the TAL activation levels must be re-set.
- **Adaptive Control Strategy (ACS) (OVTASK-152):** the tower and blade load levels ACS reacts to are set by the speed-loop response: the escalation thresholds must be set on the final loop.

- **Pitch Damage Attenuator (PDA) (OVTASK-136):** the collective pitch activity of the speed loop is the main source of pitch bearing damage at high wind: the PDA activation thresholds (pitch speed, bearing moment) depend on it.

- **Controller Overspeed Monitor (OVTASK-123):** the overspeed peaks in gusts and grid faults depend on the loop bandwidth: the overspeed limits need a margin above the peaks of the final tuning, or they alarm (too low) or protect late (too high).

- **Resonance Speed Avoider (RSA) (OVTASK-162):** RSA moves the speed-pitch reference and loop gain to cross the resonance window; its activation and mode-switch times (RSA_SpdPitCtrlActivationTime, RSA_TimePitModeSwitch) assume the speed-loop response, so they must be re-checked when the loop changes.

- **Speed Control Scheduler: Full Power State Machine (OVTASK-160):** the pitch fluctuations around the minimum pitch near rated, set by the loop, decide whether the full-power state toggles: the gap to minimum pitch and the times (FPSM_*) are set for them.
- **Tower Vibration Monitor (OVTASK-310):** the normal tower fore-aft acceleration level comes from the speed-loop response: the vibration limits must stay above it with margin.

- **Grid Fault Ride Through (GFRT) (OVTASK-301):** after a grid fault the speed loop must stop the acceleration: the post-fault gain reduction and its time window (GFRT_Post_*SpdPit*) scale the tuned PI gains.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Pitch Servo Controller (PSC) (OVTASK-132):** the pitch actuator is inside the speed loop: its bandwidth, deadband and gain schedule (PSC_Kp, Ki, KpDeadband, filters) add phase lag at the speed-loop crossover and limit the PI gains that keep a stability margin.

- **Pitch Reference Limiter (OVTASK-296):** the maximum pitch-reference rate and deadband (SpdPit_PitRefMaxRate, PitRefDeadband) bound what the speed loop can command: a rate limit hit in gusts or grid faults saturates the loop (larger speed peaks); the deadband reduces pitch activity but adds a dead zone in the loop.

- **Pitch Control States: General Pitch Rate Limits (OVTASK-131):** the general pitch-rate limits (SpdPit_MaxPitRefRatePos / Neg) bound the pitch rate of the speed loop: when they are reached the loop saturates and speed peaks grow.

- **Rotor Speed Filter (OVTASK-121):** the phase lag of the notch, low-pass and lead filters at the speed-loop crossover sets the phase margin left for the PI: changing the filters (1ES-3ES, 3P, 2T, lead) requires re-checking Kp and Ti.

- **Speed-Pitch Controller: Aerodynamic Gain Scheduling (OVTASK-125):** the PI is tuned at a reference operating point and the schedule extends it to the full-load range: a change of the schedule changes the loop gain and margins in the rest of the range, and the reverse.
- **Speed-Power Controller (PI) (OVTASK-159):** the speed-power loop bandwidth at rated sets the speed excursions the speed-pitch loop meets at the transition from partial to full load.

- **Speed Control Scheduler: Speed Shifter (OVTASK-163):** the speed shift between the pitch and power speed references (SpdShift_*) sets how far the rotor speed must rise before pitch acts: it changes the speed excursions around rated.

- **Grid Fault Ride Through (GFRT) (OVTASK-301):** the speed-pitch gain scaling during and after a grid fault (GFRT_Post_*SpdPit*) changes the effective loop gain the PI was tuned for, and so the speed recovery after the fault.
risk: Too soft: larger speed excursions, overspeed peaks, alarms or stops in gusts and grid faults, higher tower fore-aft extremes in DLC 1.4.
Too aggressive: pitch chatter and rate-limit saturation, pitch bearing and actuator damage, higher tower fatigue, interaction with the tower mode.

Gain scheduling not matched to the rotor (aerodynamic sensitivity, inertia): loss of stability margin in parts of the envelope. Grid-fault feed-forward or High Speed Gain mistuned: overspeed alarms during LVRT or near the limits.

tasks.name: Blade Load Limiter (BLL)
scope: Reduces extreme blade flap (out-of-plane) loads and tip deflection, mainly caused by extreme yaw error or turbulence: it estimates the peak out-of-plane moment of each blade and, when it exceeds a load threshold, adds a collective pitch offset to the minimum pitch limit.
Trade-off: a limited, controlled loss of aerodynamic efficiency (design rule: AEP loss at most 0.2 % in DLC 1.2a).
kpi: - Blade-root flap extreme and tip-to-tower clearance in DLC 1.2a / 1.2c and their extrapolation (DLC 1.1).
- AEP loss at most 0.2 % in DLC 1.2a.
- Activation statistics and pitch offset magnitude / duration vs wind speed.
- Robustness to blade-load sensor uncertainty (thresholds x1.08).
- [P] Pitch activity and interaction with PDA, GILL and TTCC (combined pitch offsets).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.2a normal turbulence and DLC 1.2c steep shear (flap extremes and tip clearance in normal operation, and the extrapolated extremes of DLC 1.1); DLC 1.2b and 1.2c with thresholds x1.08 (blade-load sensor uncertainty: the protection must still work with the measurement error).
**Medium:** DLC 2.4a/b extreme yaw error (large flap moments from skewed inflow, a main BLL driver); DLC 1.3 ETM; DLC 1.5 EWS (shear raises the flap moment of the upper blade).
**Lower:** DLC 1.4 ECD (gust extremes are mainly handled by GILL and TTCC).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Gust Induced Load Limiter (GILL) (OVTASK-130):** BLL and GILL both raise the minimum pitch against high flapwise loads: their thresholds and gains overlap and are tuned together so that one does not hide or double the other.
- **Controller Safe Mode (OVTASK-129):** the safe-mode derating when BLL / GILL are unavailable (SafeMode_BLLandGILL_*) must compensate their load reduction.
- **Controller Functionality Scheduler (OVTASK-135):** the priority between BLL and PDA (FuncSche_BLLPDA_PrioritizationMode) decides which pitch offset wins when both act.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Pitch Trajectory Offsets: Pitch Limit by Wind (PLBW) (OVTASK-138):** the minimum pitch at high wind reduces the thrust and the flapwise moment: BLL thresholds and gain act on the extremes left after this offset.

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the extreme flapwise moments in gusts depend on how fast the speed loop pitches out: BLL thresholds and gain are set on the extremes left after the speed loop, so a new PI tuning requires re-checking BLL.

- **Gust Induced Load Limiter (GILL) (OVTASK-130):** BLL and GILL both raise the minimum pitch against high flapwise loads: their thresholds and gains overlap and are tuned together so that one does not hide or double the other.
risk: Threshold too low: unnecessary pitch-out and AEP loss above the design rule. Threshold too high: flap extremes and tip-tower clearance not protected.
Aggressive filter dynamics: unnecessary pitch activity and actuator wear. Adverse interaction with PDA or GILL (compounded pitch-out) and shift of the operating point that raises tower loads.

tasks.name: Gust Induced Load Limiter (GILL)
scope: Mitigates tower fore-aft extreme loads in gusts: it computes a collective pitch offset from positive changes of the average blade out-of-plane moment (BLS type, GILL.AvMomCng) and adds it to the minimum pitch limit. A second type based on rotor acceleration exists but is disabled.
GILL reacts to how fast thrust increases, not to the thrust level: a transient extreme-load function that must not act in normal turbulent operation.
kpi: - Tower-base fore-aft and blade-root extremes in the gust DLCs, GILL on vs off.
- Activation in normal operation: share of time with GILL.PitchOff > 0 per wind bin in DLC 1.2a and the power-curve runs (must be minimal).
- AEP and pitch activity (RMS and max pitch rate).
- Detection timing: GILL.AvMomCng vs the gust front and clean release of the offset.
dlcs: **High:** DLC 1.4 ECD (a fast thrust rise excites the tower fore-aft mode: the design-driving tower extreme GILL is made for); DLC 2.3 EOG with grid drop (gust plus torque loss: thrust and speed rise together); DLC 9.4 extreme gusts.
**Medium:** DLC 1.2a and the power-curve runs (no activation and no AEP loss in normal turbulence); DLC 3.x start-up with EOG / EDC (gust while the rotor is accelerating); DLC 1.3 ETM.
**Lower:** DLC 1.5 EWS (shear changes are slow compared with a gust front).
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:

- **Blade Load Limiter (BLL) (OVTASK-127):** BLL and GILL both raise the minimum pitch against high flapwise loads: their thresholds and gains overlap and are tuned together so that one does not hide or double the other.
- **Controller Safe Mode (OVTASK-129):** the safe-mode derating when BLL / GILL are unavailable (SafeMode_BLLandGILL_*) must compensate the load reduction the tuned GILL gives.
- **Controller Functionality Scheduler (OVTASK-135):** the priority between GILL and PDA (FuncSche_GILLPDA_PrioritizationMode) decides which pitch offset wins when both act.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:
- **Thrust Estimator (OVTASK-153):** GILL is gain-scheduled with the normalised thrust estimate: its gains are only valid if the thrust estimate is correct at the gust conditions.

- **Pitch Trajectory Offsets: Pitch Limit by Wind (PLBW) (OVTASK-138):** the minimum pitch at high wind sets the flapwise load from which a gust starts: the gust load GILL must remove, and so its thresholds and gains, depend on this offset.

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the gust load left after the speed-loop response is what GILL has to remove: a new PI tuning changes the gust extremes and requires re-checking the GILL thresholds and gains.

- **Blade Load Limiter (BLL) (OVTASK-127):** BLL and GILL both raise the minimum pitch against high flapwise loads: their thresholds and gains overlap and are tuned together so that one does not hide or double the other.
risk: Thresholds too low or filter too fast: activation in normal turbulence, AEP loss and pitch wear. Thresholds too high or filter too slow: delayed response (about 0.1 s penalty in gust cases), tower extremes not shaved.
Poor gain scheduling: uneven load reduction over the wind-speed range. Compounded pitch-out with BLL / PDA if not coordinated.

tasks.name: Controller Overspeed Monitor
scope: Primary protection layer against rotor overspeed: two monitors on the primary and two on the secondary speed source (1 s averages) stop the turbine (Alm116031 waiting / Alm116032 stopped) before critical speeds cause extreme or fatigue loads. The secondary layer is the safety system (SRSG, Alm114041; LMU, Alm114018).
The limits are relative to the active speed reference and dynamic (DynLim01-03); the monitor also provides the time to the active limit and the active limits to other functions.
kpi: - Margin between the thresholds and the maximum 1 s-average rotor speed: low-threshold monitor at least x1.07 over normal turbulence (DLC 1.2 / 1.2a / 1.2c) and x1.05 over extreme turbulence, gusts and shear (DLC 1.3, 1.4, 1.5, 9.4c); high-threshold monitor at least x1.02 over grid drop (DLC 2.1g) and x1.05 over LVRT (DLC 2.5).
- Thresholds below the safety system (SRSG / LMU) and the converter overspeed trip, so the controller layer acts first.
- No nuisance overspeed alarm in normal operation; overspeed detected in the overspeed fault case (DLC 2.1c).
dlcs: **High:** DLC 2.1c controller overspeed (fault case: the monitor must act); DLC 2.1g grid drop and DLC 2.5a LVRT (torque loss gives the highest speed peaks: high threshold); DLC 1.2 / 1.2a / 1.2c, 1.3, 1.4, 1.5 and 9.4c (normal and extreme operation must stay below the low threshold).
**Medium:** DLC 2.2 safety-system overspeed (order of the two protection layers).
The controller overspeed monitor is disabled in most load cases, so the loads do not include its stops: the margins are checked with the monitor enabled.
affects: Functionalities whose tuning must be repeated or re-checked when the tunable parameters of this one change:
- **Safety System Overspeed (SRSG) (OVTASK-107):** the safety-system overspeed limits must sit above the controller limits, with margin, so that the controller protection acts first.
affected_by: Functionalities whose tuning changes the performance of this one to a high degree:

- **Pitch Control States: General Pitch Rate Limits (OVTASK-131):** the pitch rates in stops and at high speed error set how fast the rotor is braked aerodynamically, and so the overspeed peaks the limits must accept.

- **Speed-Pitch Controller (PI) (OVTASK-122):** the overspeed peaks in gusts and grid faults depend on the loop bandwidth: the overspeed limits need a margin above the peaks of the final tuning, or they alarm (too low) or protect late (too high).

- **Speed-Pitch Controller: Feed-Forward (OVTASK-113):** the pitch feed-forward on power-reference changes and grid faults (SpdPit_DeltaPwrToPitFFGain, SpdPit_GFRT_*FF) decides how much speed rise the faults cause: the overspeed limits must cover the remaining peaks.
- **Speed-Pitch Controller: High Speed Gain (OVTASK-124):** the High Speed Gain (SpdPit_HSG_*) raises the loop gain near the speed limits: it sets the peak speed the overspeed limits have to accept.
- **High Wind Operator (HWO) (OVTASK-154):** the curtailed speed references at high wind change the reference against which the relative overspeed limits are set.

- **Tower Acceleration Limiter (TAL) (OVTASK-139):** TAL slows the pitch-out when the tower accelerates, also in stops: slower pitch-out gives higher speed peaks, which the overspeed limits must accept.
risk: Too low: nuisance overspeed stops (availability, AEP) and extra loads from the stops. Too high: no primary protection; the safety system trips instead (harder stops, higher loads) or the design overspeed is exceeded.

couplings.reason: the selected speed source (generator or rotor speed sensor) sets the resolution, noise and delay of the measured speed: the filter chain (low-pass, notches, lead) is dimensioned for that noise and delay.
the mismatch limits (SpdMiMon_*) are set from the expected deviation between the selected speed sources.
the fused speed and the source mask (RSF_*) define which deviation between sensors is normal, which sets the mismatch limits.

the 1ES-3ES band-stop filters are centred on the ESFE estimates: the frequency range, initial frequency and threshold of ESFE decide whether the notches sit on the actual edgewise modes. A notch off the mode leaves edgewise content in the speed feedback and adds phase lag at the wrong frequency.
IPC transforms the blade moments to tilt / yaw and back with the rotor azimuth: an azimuth offset or delay rotates the tilt / yaw axes, so the IPC gain and phase are only valid for a correct azimuth.
the tower-passage window (TTCC_ActivationLvl_AziStart / AziEnd) is defined in azimuth: azimuth errors move the window away from the real tower passage.
the aerodynamic power scales with air density: the density used in the inversion of the power table sets the bias of the wind speed estimate.
the opti-pitch curve and its air-density compensation depend on the density: the optimum pitch and the thrust at a given wind speed change with it.
the estimator inverts the rotor power table (RotPerfData_PwrTbl): any error of the aerodynamic table becomes a bias of the estimated wind speed over the whole range.
the thrust estimate is read from the rotor thrust table (RotPerfData_ThrustTbl, ThrustNom).
the available power is computed from the rotor power table: table errors appear directly in the estimate.
the aerodynamic sensitivity dP/dpitch that the gain schedule compensates comes from the same rotor aerodynamics: a new rotor or new tables require a new schedule.
the optimal pitch per tip-speed ratio is the maximum of the power coefficient of the rotor tables.
the boost criteria use the rotor power table to judge the margin to rated power and loads.
the power that can be extracted during and after the inertial response is computed from the rotor power table.

the estimated wind speed is a breakpoint of the gain schedule: an estimate bias moves the scheduled gain away from the actual operating point, mainly near rated where the aerodynamic sensitivity changes fastest.
the pitch-limit-by-wind breakpoints (PLBW_WindSpd1 / 2) are defined on the estimated wind speed: a bias shifts the minimum pitch to other wind speeds, which changes thrust peaks and AEP.
the thrust estimate is a function of the estimated wind speed: its bias is passed on to the thrust.
the speed limit table (SLP_RotSpdTbl) is indexed with the estimated wind speed.
the monitor compares the measured wind speed with the estimate: the normal error band (RotPerfM_WindSpdError*) depends on the accuracy of the estimator.
GILL is gain-scheduled with the normalised thrust estimate: its gains are only valid if the thrust estimate is correct at the gust conditions.
the low-power detection compares the produced power with a percentage of the expected power: the margin (LPDC_*PercentOfPwrCrv) must cover the error of the expected power.
the rated power (PwrDesign) is the end point of the speed-power curve.
the rated power sets where the opti-pitch curve ends and pitch regulation starts.
the rated point (power and speed) is where the speed-pitch loop starts; the gain schedule is built from there to cut-out.
boost levels and conditions are defined relative to the rated power and speed.
the speed-power curve is the trajectory the speed-power loop follows in partial load: its slope sets the loop gain needed and the torque the drivetrain sees.
the curve sets the tip-speed ratio at each wind speed, and the optimal pitch is defined for that tip-speed ratio: curve and opti-pitch are designed together.
the scaling of the speed-power curve at start-up is applied to this curve.
the speed window avoided by RSA lies on the curve: the power levels at the window edges, and so the time to cross the window, depend on the curve.
the speed limited by power is a cut of the speed-power curve.
the pitch-limit-by-wind offsets (PLBW_Pit1 / 2) are added to the opti-pitch curve: a new curve changes the resulting minimum pitch and thrust.
the curtailed opti-pitch is derived from the same pitch tables; both must be consistent at the transition.
the running power curve of the estimator is computed with the opti-pitch curve.
the ACS pitch offsets (ACS_PitTbl_*) are added to the opti-pitch curve: the load reduction per offset depends on the pitch it starts from.
the pitch at rated is the first point of the gain schedule: the aerodynamic sensitivity at the start of full load depends on it.
the local power / speed limits (LocalPwrLimOEM, LocalRotSpdLimOEM) define the curtailed operating points for which the curtailed opti-pitch is designed.
the minimum pitch at high wind reduces the thrust and the flapwise moment: BLL thresholds and gain act on the extremes left after this offset.
the minimum pitch at high wind sets the flapwise load from which a gust starts: the gust load GILL must remove, and so its thresholds and gains, depend on this offset.
the boost pitch offsets (PB_*_PitMinOff) are defined relative to the minimum pitch.
the gap to the minimum pitch (FPSM_*_PitGapToMinPit) that decides the full-power state is measured from this minimum pitch.
the start pitch angle and the kick-start speeds of the operation state machine together define the aerodynamic torque and the time to reach the connection speed at start-up.
the cut-out speed and stop conditions (CutOut_RotSpd) and the stop power ramps (CutOut_*) act in the same stop: the ramp time must suit the speed at which the stop starts.

the maximum pitch-reference rate and deadband (SpdPit_PitRefMaxRate, PitRefDeadband) bound what the speed loop can command: a rate limit hit in gusts or grid faults saturates the loop (larger speed peaks); the deadband reduces pitch activity but adds a dead zone in the loop.

near rated both loops are active around the transition: their bandwidths and the speed shift between their references decide whether they hand over smoothly or fight each other.
